A marketing company combines your answers with information from other sources.
Your record becomes part of a segment based on your interests and response history.
The information passes to additional marketers or data brokers.
In the worst cases, a buyer uses the list to send deceptive prize notices or other targeted scams.
This chain can unfold without a malicious website, infected attachment or stolen password. The starting point may be a paper form sitting inside a familiar store.
Why local sweepstakes can create privacy risks

A mall kiosk or retailer drawing feels safer than a random website because you recognize the location. That familiarity can make the privacy terms easier to overlook. Before entering, look for the official rules and privacy policy. Check whether the sponsor can share your data with affiliates, sponsors or marketing partners.

Also watch for language giving permission to call, email or text you. Once several companies receive the information, tracing every copy becomes difficult. That lack of visibility is one reason a simple contest entry can create a much larger privacy footprint.
Older adults may receive targeted prize offers designed to feel personal, urgent and legitimate. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
How to protect your sweepstakes entry data
A few simple habits can limit the information you hand over, reduce unwanted marketing and help your family recognize a fake prize before money changes hands.
You cannot pull back every sweepstakes entry you have already submitted. However, you can reduce the amount of personal information available through data brokers and people-search sites.

Start by searching for your name, phone number, email address and home address online. You may find profiles that reveal your age, relatives, past addresses and other personal details. Many data brokers provide an opt-out process, although removing your information manually can take time and may require repeated requests.

You can also use a reputable data removal service to contact brokers on your behalf and continue submitting removal requests when your information reappears. Before signing up, check how many brokers the service covers, whether it offers ongoing monitoring and whether you can request removals from specific sites.

No service can erase every public record, social media post or privately held database. Still, reducing the number of sites displaying and selling your information can make it harder for marketers and scammers to build a detailed profile about you.
Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.
Get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web: CyberGuy.com.

Provide the minimum information required for a valid entry. Think twice when a form asks about your income, medications, health concerns, shopping habits or other sensitive subjects. Some promotions need your age or date of birth to verify eligibility. However, questions unrelated to the official requirements may serve a marketing purpose.
WHAT A SCAMMER SEES THE MOMENT THEY GOOGLE YOUR NAME

Look for the sponsor's full name, eligibility requirements, drawing date and privacy terms. Pay close attention to language explaining whether your information may be shared with affiliates or marketing partners. When no official rules or identifiable sponsor appear, skip the promotion.

Watch for preselected boxes or fine print that gives the sponsor permission to send promotions by email, phone or text. Leave optional marketing boxes unchecked. When consent is required to enter, decide whether the prize feels worth the additional contact and data sharing.

Consider creating an alias email address used only for contests, store loyalty programs and promotional offers. This makes follow-up marketing easier to recognize and keeps your primary inbox less exposed. A separate address cannot prevent the sponsor from sharing the information you provide. However, it can help you contain the resulting email. For more ways to protect your inbox, read how your email address gets into the wrong hands.

Do not provide a bank account number, credit card number or payment app information on a sweepstakes entry. The Postal Inspection Service advises consumers to avoid any sweepstakes requesting financial information or payment. A legitimate sponsor may need tax information after you have independently verified a major prize. That request should come after the drawing and through a confirmed company contact rather than on the original entry form.

Take a photo of a paper entry form or save a screenshot of an online promotion. Keep the official rules, sponsor name and drawing date. When someone later claims you won, compare the message with the original promotion. Contact the sponsor through information you find independently rather than using a phone number or link provided in the prize message.

The Epsilon schemes harmed many older adults and other vulnerable people. Watch for prize letters that feel urgent, personal or unusually persistent. Talk with parents and grandparents before a suspicious letter arrives. Make sure they know to call someone they trust before sending money or personal information. You can also share our guide on how to stop scam texts from targeting aging parents.

Real prizes are free. A demand for taxes, processing costs, shipping fees, gift cards, cryptocurrency or a money transfer signals a scam. Scammers often create urgency, so you have less time to question the story. Slow down and verify the company yourself. Gift card demands deserve special caution. CyberGuy has also covered how fake prizes lead to gift card losses.

Legitimate marketing emails must provide a way to opt out of future messages. Use the unsubscribe option when you recognize the company and remember signing up. Avoid clicking unsubscribe links inside suspicious messages. A fake link may lead to a phishing page or confirm that your email address remains active. Mark the message as spam and block the sender instead.

Report suspected prize or sweepstakes scams at the Federal Trade Commission's ReportFraud.ftc.gov. You can file a report even when you spotted the scam before losing money. When the scam involves the U.S. Mail, report it to the U.S. Postal Inspection Service at uspis.gov/report. The agency accepts reports involving sweepstakes, lottery and other mail fraud.
COULD THE 7-ELEVEN BREACH AFFECT YOU?
Kurt's key takeaways

That little entry card by the register can reveal far more than you think. The real concern begins when extra details leave the sponsor and become part of a marketing profile that gets shared, categorized and sold. The Epsilon case showed how lists of likely responders can become a road map for fraud, with older adults paying a steep price. Give the minimum, skip optional marketing consent and read the privacy terms before you enter. Then talk with the older people in your life before a convincing prize letter reaches their mailbox. Any prize notice demanding money belongs in the trash. You cannot pull back every old entry, but you can shrink your data trail and make your household harder to target.

title: Would this survival pod make you feel safer?
summary: LifePods survival capsules from Momentum Technologies offer flood, ballistic and earthquake protection starting around $27,000 before shipping costs.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Disaster prep used to mean bottled water, flashlights and maybe a generator in the garage. Now a French startup is taking all of that to the next level. Momentum Technologies recently showed off its LifePods survival capsules. According to the company's website, the capsules are designed to protect people, families, response teams and critical infrastructure during natural disasters, industrial risks and security threats.

You can see why something like this would get a lot of attention right now. Blackouts seem more common. Floods can move fast. Global instability has many of you wondering how prepared you really are if help cannot get there right away. LifePods takes that fear and turns it into a physical product you can buy, move and place before disaster hits.
Free live CyberGuy class: Sick of Spam? Join us July 22

Join us Wednesday, July 22, at 1 p.m. ET for a free CyberGuy Live class that will help you cut down on robocalls, spam texts, junk email and other unwanted messages. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will walk you step by step through simple ways to filter spam, clean up your inbox and recognize the messages that could put your personal information at risk. No technical experience is needed. You’ll also receive our spam-stopping checklist, and every registrant will get a link to the class recording afterward.
Reserve your free spot today at CyberGuyLive.com.
17 EMERGENCY ITEMS TO BUY BEFORE YOU ACTUALLY NEED THEM — STARTING AT $6
The LifePods B01 opens from the front, giving one or two occupants a compact shelter built for hostile environments and critical infrastructure sites. (Momentum Technologies)
What are LifePods survival capsules?

LifePods survival capsules are compact shelters built for extreme emergencies. Momentum Technologies says the capsules can provide immediate shelter during tsunamis, flash floods, storm surges, armed attacks, collapses, extreme fires and dangerous environments. That makes them different from the underground bunker you may imagine behind a hidden steel door. These capsules focus on faster deployment and a smaller footprint.

The company currently highlights two main commercial models. The W-01 is a floating capsule for water-related disasters. The B-01 is an armored land capsule for ballistic and industrial protection. Momentum also lists an earthquake-focused Q-01 concept under development.
How the LifePods B01 survival pod works

The LifePods B01 is the tougher-looking model. Momentum built it for hostile environments, critical infrastructure and situations where fast shelter could save lives. The company says the B01 gives occupants protected space against ballistic threats, fragments, armed attacks and degraded environments. It also says people can get inside and lock the system in seconds.

This model seems aimed more at security teams, industrial sites and public safety agencies than a typical backyard buyer. Momentum lists possible uses at military or police checkpoints, energy production stations, telecom hubs, transport terminals and heavy industrial sites.

The B01 lists room for one to two people, high-hardness ballistic steel, positive air filtration options and a total weight of about 4,000 pounds. Momentum says representative test panels obtained VPAM PM7 certification for resistance to 7.62x51mm military ammunition, a roughly .30-caliber rifle round. SR7 civil validation remains in progress.
How the LifePods W01 flood survival pod works
The LifePods W01 is the model that may feel more relatable if you live near water. Momentum describes it as a floating capsule for extreme weather when evacuation can no longer happen safely.

The company says the W-01 responds to risks from tsunamis, hurricanes, floods, marine submersion and dike or dam failures. It is designed to float, resist impact and keep occupants protected until rescue teams arrive. Momentum says the W-01 is designed to safely accommodate four adults. Young children may also ride with accompanying adults using additional restraint systems, similar to those used in commercial aviation.

The capsule also includes exterior grab bars. That could help survivors already in the water hold onto the outside while waiting for rescue. Every W-01 is also equipped with a geolocation and emergency distress transmission system. The goal is simple: help emergency services find the capsule faster.

The W-01 is currently completing its engineering development phase. Momentum says its structural behavior has been modeled with advanced naval engineering simulation software by Inha Works Ltd., also known as IWL, a Yamaha Motor Group company. That modeling allowed the company to evaluate structural resistance, buoyancy and stability before physical testing.

Physical validation is expected to begin during the second half of 2026. Momentum says the testing will move through initial flotation and stability tests, real-world sea trials and final certification testing in a specialized laboratory that can reproduce extreme disaster conditions such as wave impacts.
LifePods Q01 could bring protection to earthquake zones

Momentum also lists an earthquake-focused Q-01 "Quake" concept under development. That matters because earthquakes create a different kind of danger than floods or armed attacks. You may have only seconds to react, and falling debris can turn an ordinary room into a life-threatening space fast. The company says the Q-01 is being designed to provide structural protection during earthquakes. It is intended for apartments and buildings located in seismic areas.

For now, the Q-01 should be treated as a future concept rather than a product you can price out or buy today. Still, it shows where Momentum wants to take LifePods next. The company seems to be building a family of survival capsules for different disasters instead of relying on one pod to handle every threat.
15 SECURITY ESSENTIALS TO KEEP YOUR VALUABLES SAFE FOR SUMMER TRAVEL
The Q01 concept shows Momentum’s plan to expand LifePods into earthquake-focused protection beyond its land and flood survival pods. (Momentum Technologies)
Can you buy a LifePods survival pod in the U.S.?

Yes, according to Momentum. The company tells CyberGuy that U.S. customers can contact LifePods through its official website to discuss projects and place pre-orders. The first production units are expected to be available from Barcelona, Spain, in October 2026. That timing depends on the successful completion of the ongoing certification program.

For U.S. customers, deliveries are expected to begin around November 2026, depending on the final destination and shipping arrangements. The company says international shipments are planned from the Port of Barcelona. Momentum also says LifePods is represented by a U.S.-based commercial partner in San Diego, California, who can help customers through the purchasing process.

At first, the company expects demand to come mainly from government agencies, civil protection organizations, industrial operators and critical infrastructure owners. However, private customers can also reserve production capacity as the product becomes commercially available.
How much does a LifePods survival pod cost?

Momentum now lists European retail prices before VAT at 25,000 euros for the B-01 and 31,000 euros for the W-01. In U.S. dollars, that comes out to roughly $27,000 for the B-01 and about $33,500 for the W-01, depending on exchange rates. Those prices cover the capsule before shipping and other costs.

You should also expect international shipping, customs clearance, import duties, local taxes, final inland transportation and installation to add to the total. Momentum says it is finalizing its U.S. logistics strategy and expects to provide more accurate landed-cost estimates in the coming weeks. The company also says it plans to establish U.S. inventory in 2027 to reduce delivery times and improve customer support across North America. The company is also looking for strategic distribution partners across the United States to support local sales, logistics and after-sales service.
Why LifePods survival pod testing matters
The big question is proof. Trade show attention can make a product look ready for the real world. Survival gear has to do much more than look impressive under bright lights.

For the B-01, the representative armor panels have already demonstrated compliance with VPAM PM7 ballistic requirements. The remaining work focuses on validating the complete B-01 as an integrated product before it receives final VPAM SR7 certification. That distinction is important. A strong armor panel is one thing. A finished capsule with doors, ventilation, structural joints and other weak points has to prove it can hold up as a complete system.

For the W-01, Momentum says the certification program will include flotation performance, structural integrity, stability, impact resistance, self-righting capability and additional safety evaluations designed for survival equipment used during extreme natural disasters. That is the right place to focus. Flood survival depends on chaotic conditions, including debris, moving water, wave impact, panic and rescue timing.
Momentum’s LifePods lineup includes different capsule designs for emergencies ranging from floods to attacks and infrastructure failures. (Momentum Technologies)
Why LifePods says it is building survival pods now

Momentum says LifePods grew out of a simple observation after the devastating tsunamis of 2004 and 2011. The company says those disasters showed how few last-resort survival options exist once evacuation can no longer happen. The company also says LifePods are meant to complement prevention and evacuation, not replace them. Its goal is to offer a final layer of protection when every other option has failed.

That could mean armed attacks. It could mean tornadoes, hurricanes, tsunamis or catastrophic flooding. In each case, Momentum says the goal is to provide a protected space that can increase the chances of survival until emergency services arrive. The company says it sees resilient personal protection systems becoming a more important part of emergency preparedness as climate-related disasters grow more frequent and geopolitical risks continue to evolve.
Future LifePods could target fires and extreme heat

Momentum's plans go beyond the B-01, W-01 and Q-01. The company says it is also studying a FireRescue version derived from the B-01. This version would be engineered to protect occupants against intense heat and smoke during fires.

Momentum says this version would be intended mainly for emergency responders and professional users. The goal would be to provide a protected refuge while waiting for evacuation or rescue. Looking further ahead, Momentum says it is working on future autonomous LifePods that could actively regulate interior temperature. That could help occupants remain protected for longer periods under extreme environmental conditions. Ultimately, the company says its ambition is to build a complete family of survival solutions for major natural, technological and security threats.
What this means for you

LifePods taps into a feeling many of you already have. You may not want a bunker. You may not have space for one. But you probably do want a better answer for the moment when help takes too long to arrive. For now, most of you should focus on realistic emergency prep. Know your flood risk. Keep water, food and backup power available. If severe weather is a concern where you live, our storm survival essentials guide at cyberguy.com breaks down gear that can help you stay powered, connected and informed during outages.

Your phone matters too. Set up emergency contacts, Medical ID or emergency information before something goes wrong. You can also review our guide on getting your phone ready for an emergency so you know what your iPhone or Android can do when cell service fails. If you live somewhere remote or spend time outdoors, a separate satellite SOS device may also be worth considering. We have a guide to satellite communicators and emergency SOS tools at cyberguy.com that explains how they can help when your phone loses signal.

Still, LifePods shows where disaster prep may be heading. Preparedness is moving beyond small gear into bigger engineered survival systems. That could help critical sites, emergency teams and families in high-risk areas. At the same time, big claims deserve careful questions. Before anyone spends tens of thousands of dollars on a survival capsule, they should look for completed certifications, independent tests and clear installation requirements.
Kurt's key takeaways

LifePods is one of those ideas that grabs your attention because it sounds extreme at first, then starts to make sense the longer you think about it. Floods, fires, attacks and infrastructure failures can leave families and workers with very few options. I like the focus on fast shelter when evacuation becomes impossible. I also like that Momentum is thinking through different threats instead of trying to make one capsule solve every disaster. Still, I would be cautious. A survival capsule has to work when everything around it goes wrong. The latest testing update makes this feel more real than a trade show concept, but final certification will decide how strong the case really is. For now, LifePods feels like a serious emergency-tech idea with real potential, a high price tag and a lot riding on the next round of testing.
Would a survival capsule make you feel safer, or does this feel like disaster prep going too far? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: California trans suspect arrested in mother's killing after neighbor recalls heated argument
summary: Safford Wolfson, 36, was arrested on suspicion of murdering his mother Angela Caprioli at their Laguna Beach home after being named a person of interest.
story: Fox News' Bryan Llenas reports on the ongoing investigation into the murder of New Jersey mom Brooke Hanlon, found stabbed in her home. More than a month after the incident, no arrests have been made, and authorities remain tight-lipped about key details, including the 911 call and the cooperation of her husband, James Connor Hanlon. Neighbors are baffled by the unsolved case in Chester, N.J.
A California man was arrested this week in connection with his mother's killing, authorities said.

Angela Caprioli, 61, was found dead Monday at a home in Laguna Beach, according to the Laguna Beach Police Department. The New York Post identified Caprioli and the suspect, Safford Wolfson, as mother and son.
Wolfson, 36, was arrested Thursday on suspicion of murder after investigators previously identified him as a person of interest in the case.
RETIRED MATH PROFESSOR CHARGED AFTER WIFE, AN AIRLINE METEOROLOGIST, FOUND SHOT DEAD: COPS

Angela Caprioli and Safford Wolfson. Wolfson was arrested on suspicion of murder after authorities said Caprioli was found dead at a Laguna Beach home. The New York Post identified the pair as mother and son. (Angela Caprioli via Facebook)
Police said officers responded to a home in the 1300 block of Dunning Drive shortly after 11 a.m. for a death investigation and found Caprioli deceased.
The circumstances surrounding her death remain under investigation.
Neighbor Dustin Pettit said he witnessed Wolfson and Caprioli engaged in what appeared to be a heated argument at the home days before the alleged killing.
FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED AFTER SUSPECTED HUMAN REMAINS FOUND BURIED AT PROPERTY WHERE HIS FATHER LIVED
Angela Caprioli, 61, was found dead at a Laguna Beach, California, home on July 20, authorities said. (Angela Caprioli via Facebook)
"I saw her outside talking with him and it seemed like a pretty hostile conversation," Pettit told The California Post.
"She turned around and went inside and slammed the door, like she was fed up with whatever was going on."
Pettit also told CBS Los Angeles that Wolfson had moved into the home about six months earlier.

"He was pretty mysterious. He wasn't talking to us, you know, he would come outside, smoke a cigarette and play some guitar," he said. "That's kinda the extent of the relationship we've had with him over the last six months or so."

title: Illegal immigrant who killed Nashville restaurant owner to face ICE deportation after prison
summary: Ulises Raigoza-Martinez, who says he illegally entered through Texas in 2021, pleaded guilty to murdering Nashville restaurant owner Matt Carney.
story: Department of Homeland Security officials confirmed an ICE detainer has been lodged against an illegal immigrant accused of fatally crashing into two young boys in South Carolina. (WHNS)

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) are seeking custody of a Mexican citizen who authorities say entered the United States illegally through Texas in 2021 under the Biden administration and killed a Nashville restaurant owner.

After pleading guilty and being sentenced Tuesday to decades behind bars, ICE lodged an immigration detainer against Ulises Raigoza-Martinez, requesting that Tennessee officials notify the agency before his release, so federal authorities can take him into custody for removal proceedings, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

The case stems from a June 19, 2024, encounter in the parking lot of the Nashville restaurant Smokin' Thighs, where investigators claim Raigoza-Martinez stopped to steal tools from owner Matt Carney's pickup truck.
'SLAP ON THE WRIST': ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT TRUCKER'S SENTENCE IGNITES OUTRAGE AFTER CRASH KILLED 3

Matt Carney, owner of the Nashville restaurant Smokin' Thighs, died on July 4, 2024, after authorities say he was struck by a vehicle while confronting a man accused of stealing tools from his pickup truck. (DHS)

When Carney, 42, walked outside to confront the thief, Raigoza-Martinez sped away, striking the restaurateur with his vehicle, authorities said. Carney landed on the hood before being thrown to the pavement when Raigoza-Martinez turned the vehicle.
Carney suffered critical injuries and died at a Nashville hospital on July 4, 2024.

Police arrested Raigoza-Martinez in South Nashville on July 18, 2024. Two years later, on July 22, 2026, he pleaded guilty to murder, theft over $10,000, tampering with evidence and theft over $2,500, before being sentenced to 20 years in prison.
EXCLUSIVE: DHS SEEKS CUSTODY OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER TRUMP DEPORTATION, BIDEN RELEASE

Ulises Raigoza-Martinez pleaded guilty to murder, theft over $10,000, tampering with evidence and theft over $2,500 in the death of Nashville restaurant owner Matt Carney. He was sentenced to 20 years in prison. (DHS)
DHS Assistant Secretary Lauren Bis said Raigoza-Martinez "should NEVER have been in our country to commit this heinous murder."
"We will work with our state and local partners in Tennessee to ensure that he is handed over to ICE custody once his sentence is complete, so that we can remove him from our country," Bis said.
FILE - ICE is seeking custody of the suspect after he serves his prison sentence for the killing. (Paul Weaver/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

If Tennessee officials honor the ICE detainer, federal immigration authorities will take custody of Raigoza-Martinez after he completes his prison sentence so he can be placed into removal proceedings and deported.

title: Cause of death revealed for Big Sur hiker whose body was found naked on remote California trail
summary: Joanna Ruth Shields, 37, died of probable alcohol withdrawal seizures near Sykes Hot Springs in Big Sur, Monterey County investigators confirmed.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

The California hiker whose remains were found in a remote Big Sur wilderness earlier this year died from complications of alcohol withdrawal, according to the Monterey County Sheriff's Office, which ruled her death natural.
Joanna Ruth Shields, 37, died of "probable alcohol withdrawal seizures due to chronic alcohol use disorder," the sheriff's office said.

Shields was found dead April 9 near Sykes Hot Springs along the Pine Ridge Trail in Los Padres National Forest. Investigators initially treated the case as suspicious because her cause of death was unknown, and hikers reported seeing a head wound and marks on her neck.
CALIFORNIA HIKER'S BODY FOUND NAKED IN BIG SUR BACKCOUNTRY
FILE - The Monterey County Sheriff's Office ruled the hiker's death "natural." (Monterey County Sheriff's Office Facebook)
The sheriff's office said investigators found no evidence Shields was the victim of a crime.
She was found lying near a shallow creek wearing a black sports bra, with her clothing, sandals and a water bottle nearby, according to authorities.
An autopsy determined a laceration above her left eye was superficial and did not contribute to her death.
Investigators also concluded the marks on her neck were caused by postmortem insect activity and found no evidence of strangulation.
NOLAN WELLS INDEPENDENT AUTOPSY DOESN'T POINT TO FOUL PLAY, FORMER MEDICAL EXAMINER SAYS
FILE - Aerial view of Big Sur, the Santa Lucia coastal mountain range and the Los Padres National Forest, in California. (Reuters/Michael Fiala)
"Investigators found no evidence during the forensic examination or throughout the investigation to indicate that Ms. Shields was the victim of a crime," the coroner's report states.

Fox News Digital previously reported that witnesses who discovered Shields' body told local media they encountered a man who identified himself as her friend and said he had found her after the pair became separated on the trail.

At the time, Monterey County Sheriff's Office Cmdr. Andres Rosas urged the public not to jump to conclusions, saying investigators were working to determine the cause of death and that everyone at the scene had cooperated.

The coroner's report also states Shields had a history of bipolar disorder and alcohol use disorder. Family members told investigators her mental health declined in the months before her death after she stopped taking prescribed psychiatric medication. Her sister also told investigators Shields had previously experienced alcohol withdrawal seizures before becoming sober.
Monterey County Sheriff-Coroner Tina Nieto said she hopes the findings provide answers for Shields' loved ones.
FILE - The remains were found along a trail in Big Sur, California. (Brian van der Brug / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

"Our thoughts and prayers remain with Joanna's family and loved ones," Nieto said. "We hope these findings provide them with some measure of peace and closure after several difficult months."
Fox News Digital's Robert McGreevy contributed to this report.

title: NYC 'Allahu Akbar' stabbings suspect's charges revealed, yells bizarre message during perp walk
summary: Raul Morales faces attempted murder and hate crime charges after police said he stabbed two men during separate attacks on Manhattan's Upper West Side
story: A suspect accused of stabbing two men on Manhattan’s Upper West Side was captured on video yelling about justice for two unidentified people during a perp walk as investigators probe a possible hate crime.

The man accused of stabbing two people while allegedly yelling "Allahu Akbar" on Manhattan's Upper West Side Thursday afternoon has been charged with attempted murder, including hate crime counts tied to one of the victims, according to the New York City Police Department (NYPD).

During a perp walk Friday afternoon, Raul Morales, 51, could be heard yelling "Justice for the Romero family" to reporters, mentioning an unknown woman by name, and vowing, "you're going to remember her name forever."
It is unclear who the woman is, and what the possible significance is of the remarks.
According to the NYPD, Morales was being transported to Downtown Manhattan for central booking following the perp walk.
WITNESSES RECOUNT 'SCARY' NYC STABBING AFTER SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY YELLED 'ALLAHU AKBAR' DURING ATTACKS
Raul Morales, the suspect charged in two Manhattan stabbings, is escorted by NYPD officers and placed into a police vehicle following a perp walk on Friday. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News Digital)
Morales is charged with attempted murder, assault and criminal possession of a weapon in connection with the stabbing of a 57-year-old Asian man, the NYPD confirmed.
In the attack on a 50-year-old Jewish man, Morales is charged with attempted murder as a hate crime, assault as a hate crime, assault and criminal possession of a weapon.

Morales' roommate told the New York Post that the 51-year-old calmly told him he was "just going for a walk in the park" before leaving the apartment Thursday. The roommate said Morales did not appear angry or agitated before the attacks.

Neighbors who knew Morales said they were shocked by the allegations. Several residents told the New York Post they had never seen him display violent or erratic behavior in the years they had known him.
SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK

Raul Morales is walked out of the NYPD’s 20th precinct in New York, NY on Friday, July 24, 2026. Morales is the prime suspect in a double stabbing in Central Park yesterday. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News Digital)
Police said the stabbings appeared to be separate attacks that happened near each other Thursday afternoon on the Upper West Side.
Authorities said there was no known connection between Morales and either victim or between the two victims.

Investigators also executed a search warrant Friday at Morales' Upper West Side apartment as they continued to piece together a possible motive for the attacks. Police have not publicly disclosed what, if anything, was recovered during the search.
According to police, Morales allegedly yelled "Allahu Akbar" during the attacks. The NYPD is investigating whether bias played a role.
One victim is Jewish, while the other is Asian, police said.

title: Georgia high school shooting suspect Colt Gray changes plea to guilty, now faces life in prison
summary: Colt Gray, the suspect in the 2024 shooting at Apalachee High School in Georgia, now faces life in prison after entering a guilty plea on Friday.
story: Suspect Colt Gray entered a guilty plea Friday on charges related to the September 2024 shooting at Apalachee High School in Georgia, which left two students and two teachers dead.
The 16-year-old charged with killing two students and two teachers during a 2024 shooting at Apalachee High School in Georgia now faces life in prison after he entered a guilty plea Friday.

Colt Gray, who previously pleaded not guilty last October, entered the new plea Friday without reaching a deal with prosecutors. Gray, who was 14 at the time of the shooting, was charged as an adult with 55 total counts, including murder in the four deaths and 25 counts of aggravated assault. His trial had been scheduled to start in mid-October.

Teachers Richard "Ricky" Aspinwall, 39, and Cristina Irimie, 53, and students Mason Schermerhorn and Christian Angulo, both 14, died in the September 2024 shooting in Barrow County, about 45 miles northeast of Atlanta. Another teacher and eight more students were wounded, seven of them hit by gunfire.

Shayna Aspinwall, Richard Aspinwall's wife, told the judge on Friday that the "grief of losing him is constant" and lamented that the lives of their daughters, who were 2 and 5 when their father died, will be "forever marked by his absence."
FATHER OF GEORGIA HIGH SCHOOL SHOOTING SUSPECT CONVICTED OF SECOND-DEGREE MURDER, INVOLUNTARY MANSLAUGHTER

Colt Gray, the 16-year-old Apalachee High School shooting suspect, is led in by deputies for a plea hearing at Barrow County Superior Court in Winder, Ga., on Friday, July 24, 2026. (Arvin Temkar/Atlanta Journal-Constitution via AP)

Breanna Schermerhorn, whose son Mason was killed, told the judge she does not forgive Colt Gray. She said that while adults around him missed multiple warning signs, he was the one who decided to bring a gun to school and to pull the trigger.
"Those decisions were his and his alone," she said.
She described her son as someone who "made people that were typically unseen feel seen, accepted and safe" and said she was confident he would have befriended Colt Gray if he'd had the chance.

"Mason deserved a future and we all deserved a future with Mason in it, and Colt took that from Mason and everyone who loved him," she said. She and two of Mason's sisters asked the judge for a sentence of life without parole.

Before accepting the plea, Barrow County Superior Court Judge Nicholas Primm asked Gray a series of questions meant to ensure that the teenager was aware of the consequences of his plea and was entering it voluntarily. To each question, Gray responded, "Yes, your honor."
NEW VIDEO SHOWS OKLAHOMA HIGH SCHOOL PRINCIPAL TACKLING GUNMAN WHO OPENED FIRE INSIDE THE SCHOOL

Colt Gray, the 16-year-old Apalachee High School shooting suspect, stands next to his attorney Charlton Allen and pleads guilty at Barrow County Superior Court in Winder, Ga., on Friday, July 24, 2026. (Arvin Temkar/Atlanta Journal-Constitution via AP)

Because he pleaded guilty to murder, Gray faces a minimum sentence of life in prison, according to The Associated Press. The judge must decide whether he should be eligible for parole after hearing victim statements, evidence and each side's summary of the case.
Gray sat at a table in the courtroom with his feet chained together next to his attorney. Members of the community, including some victims and family members, were present in the courtroom.
A jury in March convicted his father, Colin Gray, of charges including second-degree murder and involuntary manslaughter, and he is scheduled to be sentenced next week.

Prosecutors successfully argued that Colin Gray provided his son with the AR-15-style rifle used in the attack as a Christmas gift, continued buying him ammunition, despite being aware of his mental health deterioration and prior school shooting threats investigated by law enforcement.

Colin Gray looks down and to the side as the guilty verdict is read in Barrow County Superior Court on March 3, 2026. Gray was later handcuffed and led from the courtroom after being convicted of second-degree murder and involuntary manslaughter. (WAGA)

The prosecution told jurors that despite those concerns, Gray did not pursue inpatient treatment for his son.

title: Man accused of raping three underage girls faces new charge from prison
summary: Imarr Finley, facing rape charges involving three underage girls in Harrisburg, now faces vandalism charges after allegedly breaking a Dauphin County Prison window.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A man awaiting trial for allegedly raping three underage girls is facing new charges after reportedly breaking a window inside a Pennsylvania prison.

Imarr Finley, 25, of Harrisburg, Pa., has been at the jail since December 2024, when he was arrested after allegedly kidnapping a 12-year-old girl on her way home from school, taking her to his home and raping her, according to court records obtained by Pennlive.com.
Court records show Finley was charged with the rape of two other girls. One girl was 17, while the other was 13 or 14, Pennlive.com reported.

Finley's most recent criminal charge stems from a July 8 incident when he allegedly broke a control room window on the Dauphin County Prison's P block while he was out of his cell on recreation time, according to a probable cause affidavit obtained by Pennlive.com.
FLORIDA MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY LURED WOMEN WITH DATING APP COULD HAVE MORE VICTIMS: AUTHORITIES
Imarr Finley shown in a mugshot photo shortly after his arrest in December 2024 for the alleged rape and kidnapping of a 12-year-old girl in Harrisburg, Pa. (Harrisburg Police Department)
The affidavit, filed by the Dauphin County District Attorney’s Office, claimed two corrections officers saw Finley break the window, which caused $772 in damage.
Court records show Finley was charged on Thursday with institutional vandalism, a second-degree misdemeanor.
For that charge, he was arraigned on Thursday afternoon and a preliminary hearing has been scheduled for Aug. 4. Fox News Digital reached out to the prison for comment.
The first alleged rape occurred on Nov. 25, 2024, in the uptown Harrisburg area, according to police.
According to Pennlive.com, the girl told authorities that a man dressed in all black and a mask over his face was following her.
An undated photo of Dauphin County Prison, the facility where Finley is incarcerated and where he allegedly broke a cell block window. (Dauphin County Prison)
FORMER PRISON GUARD WHO HAD SEX TAPE WITH INMATE GO VIRAL IS FILLED WITH REGRET & NOW FOCUSING ON BEING A MOM

The man, who police say was Finley, got the girl to follow him to his house, where he allegedly raped her and threatened the girl's family if she told anyone, Pennlive.com reported. Days later, on Dec. 4, 2024, Finley was arrested by Harrisburg police after he fled out the second story window of a home and tried to flee by running across rooftops, according to authorities.
On March 23, 2026, Finley was charged in connection with the rape of a 13- or 14-year-old girl who he allegedly lured to his house with a fake Snapchat photo, Pennlive.com reported.
Dauphin County Prison sign (Dauphin County Prison)

Four days later, he was charged with raping a 17-year-old girl after authorities said DNA evidence tied him to the crime, according to the outlet.
Finley is being held without bond and is due to appear in court for the rape charges on July 30.

title: Jewish leaders fault Mamdani rhetoric as Upper West Side stabbing, hate crime probe continues
summary: Jewish leaders in New York City are speaking out against Mayor Zohran Mamdani's rhetoric as an investigation continues into a potential hate crime.
story: Eric Goldstein, the CEO of the UJA-Federation of New York and Rabbi Yosie Levine of The Jewish Center speak about New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's rhetoric, as a hate crime probe continues following a stabbing in Manhattan.

Jewish leaders in New York City are accusing Mayor Zohran Mamdani of "fanning the flames of hatred and division" as an investigation is continuing Friday into a pair of stabbings in Manhattan’s Upper West Side that are being looked at as potential hate crimes.

New York Attorney General Letitia James said both victims in Thursday’s attack are currently in stable condition. The suspect, identified as Raul Morales, 51, is accused of yelling "Allahu Akbar" while stabbing two men on Thursday afternoon, according to officials.

"When the mayor of New York repeatedly uses his platform to relentlessly single out and demonize Israel, the world's only Jewish state, and calls those who support it monsters, he contributes to a climate in which Jewish New Yorkers are increasingly targeted and unsafe," Eric Goldstein, the CEO of the UJA-Federation of New York, said Friday.

"Mayor Mamdani, stop fanning the flames of hatred and division. The consequences are not abstract. They are playing out on our streets. But make no mistake, we're not going anywhere. The Jewish community of New York, the largest in the world outside Israel, will continue to walk the streets of the Upper West Side and all the streets of New York openly and proudly," he added.
SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a still image taken from handout video released on July 21, 2026. (Reuters)

Rabbi Yosie Levine of The Jewish Center also said Friday that, "When public officials repeatedly cast the Jewish community as a stand-in for actions of the Israeli government, they create a climate in which Jews become targets."

"You know when I was growing up, the only time we saw security outside of my synagogue or outside of my Jewish day school was when the mayor came to speak. The police were there to protect him. Today, every time the mayor speaks, we need the police to protect us," he added. "Jewish life in America is starting to feel like Jewish life in Europe. Armed guards, bulletproof glass, and the constant fear that yesterday's rhetoric will turn into today's assault."

When asked by Fox News Digital for a response, Mamdani's office highlighted remarks the mayor made to NY1 on Friday, in which he said, "There's no tolerance for antisemitism or hatred of any kind in this city."

"This is a city that believes in the beauty and the breadth of all of its five boroughs and everyone who calls it home. And if anyone is perpetrating this kind of a bigotry, that kind of hatred, they will be held fully accountable," Mamdani told the station.

"When it comes to my comments about Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, they are critiques not based on my personal analysis but rather on objective facts," he added. "They are critiques of a political leader not of people of a specific faith or a religion or a background and my responsibility as the mayor of this city is to keep every New Yorker safe, no matter where they come from, what they believe in, or frankly, even if they agree with my politics. My job is to keep them safe."
WITNESSES RECOUNT 'SCARY' NYC STABBING AFTER SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY YELLED 'ALLAHU AKBAR' DURING ATTACKS
The suspect allegedly yelled "Allahu Akbar" during the attack on Thursday, July 23, in New York City. (Manhattan Shomrim Safety Patrol/@AGHamilton29 via X)
The victims were identified in media reports as Chok Sung, 57, and Moshe Grunhaus, 50.

"So many people know Moshe, so many people care about him. He was just trying to pray at his synagogue, and now we're the ones praying for his recovery," Levine said. "To have been stabbed 200 feet from the Jewish center evokes all the worst images of the Jewish past. If a Jew can't feel safe walking home from shul in broad daylight on a Thursday afternoon on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, then something has gone profoundly wrong, not only for the Jewish community, but for our city."
Goldstein added that Mamdani's recent video in which he called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "war criminal" was "political grandstanding."

"This is the largest Jewish community in the world outside of Israel. His words have profound real world consequences on us and shame on him. Shame on him for doing this for perceived political benefit when it has real world consequence for the Jews of New York. He must stop," Goldstein said.
James said after speaking with the NYPD commissioner and local district attorney, "they have asked me not to draw any conclusions as a result of last night's event."

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said that while his office lacks the authority to arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu under the International Criminal Court's warrant, he urges the U.S. to do so. (Camara Porter/AdMedia/Sipa USA; Ronen Zvulun/Pool/Reuters)
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP

"What I do want to say is that it's really critically important that individuals understand that anti-Semitic acts have been growing in the city of New York. It's really critically important," she said. "And then also acts against the Asian community have also been on the increase. So it's important that I stand with my Jewish friends, that I stand with my Asian friends, that I let everyone know that there should not be any space between any of us, that we should stand together against any form of hate, any act of hate in the city and the state of New York, that it will not be tolerated."
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Lindsay Clancy judge shields 911 call, autopsy photos in mom’s triple-murder trial
summary: Patrick Clancy's 911 call and autopsy photos of his three children will be shielded from public broadcast as Lindsay Clancy's murder trial begins.
story: Criminal defense attorney David Gelman offers insights into the impending Lindsay Clancy trial, where opening statements are set for Monday. Gelman examines Patrick Clancy's motion to keep sensitive evidence, like 911 calls and children's photos, from the public. He highlights the emotional toll on the jury and the complex defense of potential postpartum depression.

A Massachusetts judge has partially granted a grieving father’s request to shield some of the most graphic evidence expected to surface at the murder trial of his now-ex-wife, who is accused of strangling their three young children inside the family’s home.

Plymouth Superior Court Judge William Sullivan ruled Friday that the media and public may not record, display, reproduce or distribute Patrick Clancy’s initial 911 call or autopsy photographs of 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan Clancy.
The evidence may still be presented to jurors during Lindsay Clancy’s trial, which is set to begin Monday with opening statements.
LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN
Reporters may also describe what is heard or shown in court but cannot broadcast or publish the recording or images themselves, according to the two-page order.

Lindsay Clancy, charged with the murder of her three children in Duxbury in 2023, appears in Plymouth Superior Court on Friday, Feb. 20, 2026. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

Patrick Clancy had asked Sullivan to restrict the public and media’s ability to record, broadcast or distribute evidence, including the 911 call, family and crime-scene photographs, autopsy images and the clothing the children were wearing.

Sullivan’s order specifically bars the reproduction or dissemination of the 911 recording and autopsy photographs. It does not prevent prosecutors or the defense from introducing the evidence at trial.
Sullivan wrote that the release or reproduction of the material would create a "substantial likelihood of harm" or another harmful consequence for Patrick Clancy and the children’s family.
Lindsay and Patrick Clancy with two of their three children in this undated photo (Lindsay Marie Clancy/ Facebook)

Sullivan issued the ruling after hearing arguments from attorneys representing Patrick Clancy, prosecutors and Lindsay Clancy. Boston Globe Media Partners also filed a response opposing aspects of the request, according to the order.

title: Eleven indicted in alleged Texas smuggling scheme that left 7 migrants dead in shipping container
summary: Seven migrants died trapped inside a shipping container on a Union Pacific train in Texas, with a 14-year-old among the victims of the smuggling ring.
story: U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons said the illicit border crossing scheme led to the deaths of seven illegal migrants. (Credit: KABB)

Eleven people were indicted this week for allegedly participating in a years-long human smuggling operation that left seven illegal migrants dead in May after they were trapped for hours inside an unventilated shipping container in Texas.

Prosecutors say the migrants were loaded into the container near Del Rio before it was transported by train across the state. Six were later found dead inside it in Laredo and a seventh was discovered near railroad tracks at the San Antonio stop, according to authorities.
The victims — four Mexican nationals and three Honduran nationals — had no chance of escape because the container could not be opened from the inside, according to prosecutors.

"The ultimate destination for these aliens who began their journey in Del Rio was likely San Antonio. Once the train got to San Antonio, this alien smuggling organization that facilitated the movement of these individuals opened the train car doors," U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons said at a press conference on Friday.
SIX ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, INCLUDING 14-YEAR-OLD, FOUND DEAD IN SHIPPING CONTAINER ALONG SOUTHERN BORDER
The container the migrants were found dead in at the Laredo rail yard in Texas in May 2026. (U.S. Attorney's Office Western District of Texas)

"There was one individual inside that then fell out of the car. They left that individual for dead there by the tracks in San Antonio, closed the door to the container and sent the train on its way, the train ultimately ending up in Laredo, Texas, where the other six bodies were found," Simmons added.
One of the victims was a 14-year-old child, while another individual inside the car "frantically contacted their family as they were dying from the sweltering heat in that container," Simmons said.

The 11 defendants — four of them from the U.S. and seven from either Mexico, Honduras or Guatemala — allegedly ran a human smuggling organization from around April 2023 until May 2026, according to the indictment.
The group allegedly used cargo trains to get migrants further into the interior of the U.S. after getting them across the border, per the indictment.
Union Pacific Rail Yard in Laredo, Texas, where six of the migrants smuggled into the U.S. were found dead. (U.S. Attorney's Office Western District of Texas)
MEXICAN NATIONAL SENTENCED IN BORDER CHILD SMUGGLING CASE INVOLVING THC-LACED CANDY
Prosecutors allege that toward the end of April this year, the organization began facilitating the travel of the group of seven migrants who would later die in the shipping container.
Each of the victims paid the smugglers between $1,500 and $10,000 to be transported from Acuña, Mexico, into the U.S., according to the indictment.

On the afternoon of May 9, the migrants made it into Del Rio, where the smugglers allegedly used a bolt cutter to snap the lock off a Conex shipping container that was aboard a stationary Union Pacific train, prosecutors said.
Once inside the container, the migrants were dealing with outside temperatures of 88 to 92 degrees Fahrenheit, according to investigators.
The train traveled along U.S. 90 to San Antonio, about 150 miles away from Del Rio, where the smugglers caught up with the migrants and found them "in peril," prosecutors said.
Map of train route from Del Rio, Texas, to San Antonio. (U.S. Attorney's Office Western District of Texas)
‘BAKED TO DEATH’: HOMAN RIPS MEDIA WHILE SHARING HORRIFIC SCENES FROM BORDER ENFORCEMENT CAREER

According to the indictment, the smugglers that were there allegedly left one of the migrants who had already died near the railroad tracks before abandoning the rest of the migrants inside the shipping container as it traveled to Laredo.
The next day, a worker at the Union Pacific Railyard in Laredo saw a leg sticking out of the container, leading to the discovery of the dead migrants, the indictment said.
San Antonio authorities later discovered the body of the migrant who had been left by the railroad tracks, prosecutors said.
Nine of the 11 people charged in connection with the smuggling and the deaths of the migrants have been arrested and are now in federal custody.
Mayra Alejandra Huerta, 32, of Del Rio, was the first to be arrested on May 12.
Karina Garcia, 37, of Del Rio, is one of the defendants that has not been arrested. (U.S. Attorney's Office Western District of Texas)
Last week, eight other defendants charged in the indictment were arrested in central and south Texas as part of a Homeland Security Task Force operation.
Those arrested from the U.S. were Edson Alejandro Perez, 18, of Del Rio; and Eric Hernandez, 40, of Eagle Pass, Texas.
Another two defendants arrested were from Honduras — Jonas Ulloa-Aguilera, 25, and Franklin Williams Ayala Aguilera, 30.
Three more were from Mexico — Maria Norma Neri de Moran, 56; Damian Huerta Analucas, 55; and Rosario Cristal Lopez-Saldana, 26.
Finally, Pascual Raymundo Loarca, 34, of Guatemala, was also arrested in the Homeland Security operation.
Seferino Huerta-Casillas, 35, of Mexico, is another defendant who has yet to be apprehended. (U.S. Attorney's Office Western District of Texas)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Two of those charged remain at large, including 37-year-old Karina Garcia of Del Rio and 35-year-old Seferino Huerta-Casillas of Mexico.

All the defendants were charged with one count of conspiracy to transport illegal aliens resulting in death and one count of aiding and abetting transport of illegal aliens resulting in death. They face a maximum of life in prison.

title: 'America's Most Wanted' ex-cop fugitive returned after 20 years on the run to face murder, child sex charges

A former South Carolina police officer accused of killing his wife before disappearing for more than two decades has been returned to the United States from China to face murder and child sex charges, the U.S. Marshals Service announced Thursday.

title: Illinois worker spent over six hours trapped in gas station sign too tall for fire truck ladders to reach
summary: AJ Gow spent over six hours trapped inside a 130-foot gas station sign in Wilmington, Illinois, after his boom lift malfunctioned during repair work.
story: The worker was trapped after his lift malfunctioned, leading to a massive emergency response. (Credit: WFLD)
An Illinois maintenance worker was trapped for more than six hours in a 130-foot-tall gas station sign after his lift malfunctioned.
The worker, who identified himself as AJ Gow, was doing repair work Tuesday on the towering sign, which is located along Lorenzo Road off Interstate 55 in Wilmington.
At 1:55 p.m., the Wilmington Fire District was called to this area on a report of a worker stuck inside one of the enclosed signs atop the sign pole.
EIGHT RIDERS LEFT DANGLING ATOP 100-FOOT ROLLER COASTER FOR OVER THREE HOURS AT TEXAS AMUSEMENT PARK

Fire crews with the Wilmington Fire District in Illinois ascend a boom lift to rescue a maintenance worker, AJ Gow, who was trapped inside one of the signs atop the 130-foot pole for hours on Tuesday. (Wilmington Fire District)

"The telescopic boom lift used by the worker had malfunctioned and Fire District personnel were told he had been at the elevated position for around 3 hours," officials with the fire district said in a statement on social media.
Additionally, the sign pole had no stairs or ladders built into it, making it impossible for rescue teams to climb up without another lift, officials said.
Another problem was that the Wilmington Fire District's trucks have ladders that only go 100 feet in the air, which meant Gow was 30 feet out of reach.

Eventually, fire officials located another boom lift in the Joliet area, which is roughly 20 miles north of the rest stop. The lift was brought to the sign with an Illinois State Police escort, officials said.
AJ Gow, the worker, said he spent over six hours trapped in the interior of the sign after his lift malfunctioned. (Wilmington Fire District)
FAMILY'S SPRING BREAK HIKE TURNS INTO LIFE-OR-DEATH RESCUE AFTER PARENT FALLS 70 FEET OFF UTAH CLIFF
After the new lift was in place, firefighters were able to reach Gow and get him back to the ground, the fire district said.
Gow thanked all the first responders from different departments that came to his aid, saying that "seeing that lift roll up with police escorts was the highlight of my day for sure!!"
Gow later said on social media that he spent over six hours in a cramped position within the interior of the sign.
An aerial view of the sign AJ Gow was trapped in for more than six hours this week. (WFLD)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"I was too hot and thirsty to be anxious. I was moreso nauseous and dizzy. And incredibly uncomfortable to be in for over 6 hours. It was only 16" wide and wasn't even tall enough to stand fully upright either," Gow wrote in response to someone commenting on the fire district's post.
In another comment, Gow said the sign "kept swaying with the wind."
Gow said that after he got down, he went to the hospital to be treated for dehydration. Fox News Digital reached out to Gow for comment.

title: Purported Nancy Guthrie note includes unusual demand that breaks basic ransom rule: retired FBI negotiator
summary: A retired FBI negotiator says the first ransom note in the Nancy Guthrie Tucson kidnapping case is inconsistent with a typical ransom motive.
story: New excerpts from a purported Nancy Guthrie ransom note appear inconsistent with the kidnapping-for-ransom motive, according to retired FBI negotiator and supervisory agent Jason Pack.
The latest revelations about the purported first ransom note in the Nancy Guthrie case appear inconsistent with a kidnapping for ransom, according to a retired FBI negotiator.

"The fact that they wanted to cut off communication quickly suggests that they may not have had kidnapping for ransom as a primary motive, even though that's what this says," said Jason Pack, a retired FBI supervisory agent. "It doesn't seem like how a usual kidnapping goes down."

He said typical kidnappers want to keep communication channels open to negotiate payment and maintain leverage over the victim's family, making the reported demand for no further contact highly unusual.
NEW DETAILS FROM NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMAND REVEALED, 'HER LIFE IS IN YOUR HANDS': REPORT
Savannah Guthrie will return to "Today" on Monday after a two-month absence since her mother, Nancy, went missing on Feb. 1. (Getty Images/Fox News Digital)
"The most telling sign is this no negotiation, no further contact line," Pack told Fox News Digital. "Genuine kidnappers wanna keep the line of communication open."

The sender did, however, incorporate known pressure tactics, including setting a deadline, making threats and telling the family that Guthrie knew what would happen if they failed to comply, Pack said.
But cutting off communication before the deadlines passed was also unusual, he added.
NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM NOTE CLAIMED THAT SHE HAD DIED, BEEN ‘BURIED WITH NATURE,’ SOURCE SAYS
Annie Guthrie, her husband Tommaso Cioni, and Savannah Guthrie at their missing mother Nancy Guthrie's home on Monday, March 2, in Tucson, Arizona. (Fox News)

Guthrie was taken from her home in Tucson's Catalina Foothills neighborhood in the early morning hours of Feb. 1, according to the Pima County Sheriff's Department and the FBI. She has not been seen since, and no proof of life was ever provided.
In a second purported ransom note, the sender indicated Guthrie had died soon after she was taken and been buried "with nature."
New excerpts from what is reportedly the first note received by local media shed light on why Pack believes the communication departed from a traditional ransom demand.
NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM NOTES DON'T MATCH SUSPECT'S BEHAVIOR, PROFILER SAYS: 'I DON'T BELIEVE THEY'RE REAL'
These two images were released by the FBI, recovered from Nancy Guthrie's Nest doorbell camera. It's unclear whether they show the same person. (FBI)

Briana Whitney, who was working for the Phoenix-based AZ Family news outlet when the case broke, joined "Crime Junkie" host Ashley Flowers on Wednesday to discuss the note her former outlet received. "Crime Junkie" declined to share copies of the text.

"Hello Savannah, we have your mother Nancy," she began, reading from what she said was the first note sent to local media. "She is safe but scared. She will be held for ransom, and once payment is received, she will be released unharmed. We will be holding her for a maximum of seven days."
As previously conveyed by authorities, the sender gave two deadlines with increased money demands the longer it took.

"Once payment is received to the Bitcoin address below, she will be released within 12 hours of deposit to a safe drop-off location back in Tucson," Whitney read. "If the payment is not received by the last deadline on Monday the 9th at 5 p.m., she will be killed. Your mother is aware of this, and her life is in your hands."

Deputies examine a flyer taped to Nancy Guthrie's mailbox on Sunday, Feb. 22, 2026. They were called to the scene after volunteer searchers and several streamers walked onto Guthrie's property with a shovel. (Michael Ruiz/Fox News Digital)
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
The sender left no room for further dialogue.

"It is in the best interest of everyone to have this completed as soon as possible," the note reportedly continued. "You will not be able to contact me from here on out. There will be no negotiation. Do not play games. Law enforcement will not be able to help you."
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

The note also included details that may have only been available to investigators and the suspect at the time, including the location of Guthrie's Apple Watch and details about the smashed floodlight in her backyard — but even that is not enough to pin down kidnapping for ransom as a motive, Pack said.
Savannah Guthrie poses alongside her mother Nancy Guthrie during a production break whilst hosting NBC's "Today" show live from Australia. (Photo by Don Arnold/WireImage)

"The details about the security camera and the spotlight that was out, that proves that they know what the home was like, what the environment may have been like, but it's not a real proof of life," he said.
SEND US A TIP
In most ransom kidnappings, he said, the abductors will want to prove they have possession of the victim and that the victim is alive.
"All these things put together don't seem really like they go with the kidnapping for ransom," he said.

Investigators appear to be split on the notes' authenticity. While one person has already pleaded guilty to sending an impostor ransom note to Guthrie's other daughter, Annie, and her husband Tommaso Cioni, that case is not believed to be connected to the notes sent to local media stations.

A well-wisher signs a banner that reads "Bring her home" and shows a photo of Nancy Guthrie, U.S. television journalist Savannah Guthrie's abducted elderly mother, at the KVOA newsroom, where Savannah worked earlier in her career, in Tucson, Arizona, Feb. 12, 2026. (Rebecca Noble/Reuters)

"The FBI and its task force partners have received several ransom notes over the course of this investigation," the FBI's Phoenix office said in a statement in June. "Some have been deemed to be extortion attempts without legitimacy. Other ransom demands may potentially be legitimate and are still being investigated as such. This case continues to be investigated as a kidnapping for ransom case. The FBI has and will continue to offer all assistance possible in the investigation — however local authorities remain the lead."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Some investigators said they were confident that the ransom demands are all bogus, while others are cautious about reaching that conclusion while Guthrie's whereabouts remain unknown, federal law enforcement sources told Fox News and Fox News Digital. Still, the two notes that Whitney mentioned have been deemed potentially authentic by investigators and by the Guthrie family.
The only known suspect remains publicly unidentified — a masked intruder who appeared on Nest doorbell camera video that the FBI recovered with help from Google.
He is described as standing between 5 feet, 9 inches and 5 feet, 10 inches tall with an average build. He was wearing a black Ozark Trail backpack. It remains unclear whether he acted alone.

title: Good Samaritan in Spider-Man costume helps man in wheelchair cross busy intersection in viral moment
summary: Video from Jonesboro, Arkansas, traffic cameras captured a driver in a Spider-Man costume helping a person in a wheelchair cross an intersection.
story: Christopher Hellenthal, 20, seen on video leaping out of vehicle to help a man in Jonesboro, Arkansas. (Credit: Jonesboro Police Department/TMX)
A good Samaritan wearing a Spider-Man costume was captured on video leaping out of his vehicle to help a man in a wheelchair cross a busy intersection in Arkansas in a moment that has gone viral.
The heartwarming scene was filmed by traffic cameras on Tuesday after Christopher Hellenthal, 20, said he clocked out of work at a trampoline park in Jonesboro.

"That morning we had a superhero day, and so I brought it for the toddlers, and they had a blast," Hellenthal said about the Spider-Man costume. "And whenever I got off work and clocked out, I was actually just going to head into town and just kind of drive around with the suit. And I noticed that there was this man, and he was in a wheelchair, and he was having a lot of trouble, he wasn’t going to make it."

"But I just got out real fast, and I just helped him along, adrenaline pumping through me. I just told the man, I said, ‘don’t worry I got you,’ and I guess he understood, and I got him to a safe spot, and I made it back to my vehicle and just drove off," he added.
CRUISE PASSENGER HAILED AS HERO AFTER JUMPING INTO WATER TO SAVE 84-YEAR-OLD MAN
Christopher Hellenthal, 20, who is dressed in a Spider-Man costume, is seen in Jonesboro, Ark., helping a man in a wheelchair cross a busy intersection. (Jonesboro Police Department/TMX/AP)
"I would have done it with or without the suit," Hellenthal also said.
The moment was shared on the Facebook page of the Jonesboro Police Department, which called Hellenthal a "true superhero."
"We were able to spot this little web of kindness on our intersection cameras. Thank you, sir, for helping this gentleman reach his destination safely," police said.
Sally Smith, a police department spokesperson, told The Associated Press that "Not in my 7 years in the department have I witnessed this."
'PRO-LIFE SPIDERMAN' SENTENCED TO PRISON FOR CLIMBING LAS VEGAS SPHERE
Hellenthal said he would have helped the man "with or without the suit." (Jonesboro Police Department/TMX/AP)

Hellenthal, who lives in Lake City, east of Jonesboro, said he's always been a Spider-Man fan. He told the AP that he even had the opportunity to meet the late Stan Lee, one of the character’s co-creators.
Packy Magel, a manager at Ultimate Air Trampoline Park who works with Hellenthal, said he recognized Hellenthal from the video despite his superhero getup.
The video ends with Hellenthal helping the man cross the intersection on Tuesday, July 21, 2026, in Jonesboro, Ark. (Jonesboro Police Department/TMX/AP)

It’s "very much like him to do something like that and very much like him to be still in costume," Magel said to the AP.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Governor blames activists in Nolan Wells case for ‘stoking division,’ official says FBI probing threats
summary: The FBI is investigating threats against witnesses and authorities in the Nolan Wells case as Mississippi's governor blames Ben Crump and Al Sharpton, an official said.
story: Mississippi Department of Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell said threats against public officials, witnesses and the Wells family are being taken 'very, very seriously' in an interview with Russ Latino from Mississippi Public Broadcasting.

MISSISSIPPI – The FBI is investigating threats against the people who were with Nolan Wells in the hours before the Mississippi teen vanished and was found dead, one of the state's top law enforcement officials says.

Wells, 18, disappeared July 4 after joining friends on a boat trip to Horn Island, a barrier island off Mississippi's Gulf Coast. Search crews scoured the area for two days before a National Park Service ranger found his remains on the island's northwestern tip on July 6.

Mississippi Department of Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell said Wednesday that the FBI is investigating threats made against public officials, the people who were with Wells before he vanished and their families. Tindell made the comments on Mississippi Public Broadcasting's "The Sit Down" hosted by Magnolia Tribune Founder and CEO Russ Latino.
NOLAN WELLS' HOMETOWN OFFICIALS RALLY BEHIND SHERIFF AFTER 'DERELICT IN THEIR DUTIES' ATTACK
Nolan Xavier Wells disappeared on the Fourth of July while boating with friends, according to authorities. (Jackson County Sheriff's Department via Facebook)

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Tindell said "false information" shared about Wells' death has incited "rage and emotion" that has led to a higher level of calls coming into his office, some of which are "direct threats." Tindell said he believes Wells' mother, Christine Wonsley, has also received threats.

"I can tell you, the FBI has reached out. They're working in any capacity. They've offered a hand, in this case, to do anything that that's needed from their end. But they're also taking a serious look, at some of these threats that have come across, to public officials, to witnesses to the family, to anybody involved in this case," Tindell said.
Tindell confirmed to Fox News Digital that such threats are being investigated.

"I can confirm that we have had threats made against DPS employees and those threats are being actively investigated. Some potential witnesses and their families have also received threats and those are being investigated as well," he said.
NOLAN WELLS INDEPENDENT AUTOPSY DOESN'T POINT TO FOUL PLAY, FORMER MEDICAL EXAMINER SAYS
Nolan Wells smiles on the field while playing wide receiver for Southwest Mississippi Community College. (Christine Wonsley/Facebook)

The warning from one of Mississippi's top public safety officials comes as national attention on the case has reached a fever pitch, with Rep. André Carson, D-Ind., accusing officials in Mississippi of not being transparent.

"Not only are [Nolan Wells' family] suffering the unimaginable grief of losing a child, they're not getting the truth, transparency, or accountability. Mississippi officials retained some of Nolan's body parts, so yesterday's independent autopsy leaves more questions unanswered," Carson said.

As the speculation has grown, Mississippi's top elected officials have begun pushing back publicly.
SEARCH CALLED OFF AFTER BODY MATCHING MISSING TEEN NOLAN WELLS FOUND OFF MISSISSIPPI COAST
Republican Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves told Fox News Digital in a statement that attorney Ben Crump and Al Sharpton are responsible for inciting the threats.

"Ben Crump and Al Sharpton are to blame for the threats. They are stoking division for personal gain. It’s sad to see, but not unexpected. This is how they’ve built their careers," Reeves said. I’m confident they will follow the facts of the case, wherever that leads them. The state's top prosecutor is also drawing a hard line."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch told Fox News Digital in a statement that her office will hold accountable anyone who threatens law enforcement working the case.

"I am proud of the professionalism with which our law enforcement, district attorney, and other local leaders are approaching this tragic case. During an open investigation, it is vital to the cause of justice that everyone respect the integrity of the process. Efforts to intimidate, disrupt, or interfere with the work of our law enforcement and prosecutors and threats to their well-being will be taken seriously and we will hold those who make them accountable. During Wednesday's news conference, Crump revealed that an area of "red discoloration" was found on Wells' head, but said Dr. Roger Mitchell, who performed the autopsy, couldn't come to a conclusion on a cause or manner of death "pending further investigation." An official autopsy into Wells' death hasn't been completed, but the revelation from Crump fueled even more speculation.

Wells' friends returned to the mainland that July afternoon without him, but Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter previously said investigators believe Wells chose to stay on the island. It wasn't until later that night that his mother learned he was missing from one of Wells' friends and reported it to authorities.
The FBI told Fox News Digital in a statement it's working with local law enforcement to investigate the threats.

The FBI will remain ready to assist JCSO Investigators as they request our support, particularly when federal resources may expand their capacity to provide clarity and peace of mind for Nolan’s loved ones," the agency said.
