title: Wisconsin protester brands Madison as 'corrupt city' during anti-police tirade following deadly shooting
summary: A Madison police briefing on the deadly shooting of a homeless man was interrupted when a protester grabbed the podium, denounced police and called the city "corrupt."
story: Madison Police Chief John Patterson said "I'll step aside" and allowed a protester to take over the microphone during an update on the fatal police shooting of Corey Ruiz. Police said Ruiz was armed with a knife.

A Wisconsin police briefing descended into chaos Thursday when a protester seized the podium during a heated demonstration that interrupted officials discussing the fatal police shooting of a homeless man.
The briefing came one day after law enforcement officers shot and killed a homeless man who authorities said wounded an officer with a knife during an encounter Wednesday.
According to officials, officers were responding to reports of a person stealing bicycles and checking vehicle doors. Police identified the man as Corey Durell Ruiz, a 38-year-old homeless resident.
Police said Ruiz was armed with a knife and injured an officer, but protesters accused law enforcement of using excessive force and invoked the 2020 death of George Floyd.
FBI ARRESTS PROTESTER WHO THREATENED TO KILL ICE OFFICER'S FAMILY AT NJ DETENTION CENTER PROTEST, BLANCHE SAYS
A protester took over a police briefing in Madison, Wisconsin, on July 23, 2026, following a police-involved shooting incident.  (City of Madison)
One demonstrator then grabbed the microphone from Police Chief John Patterson.
"We don’t want any of that talk," a protester said.

The protester then delivered a lengthy denunciation of police, capitalism, imperialism and Zionism, accusing Patterson of participating in a system that he said had oppressed his family for generations.
While the disruption continued, another demonstrator held up a sign that read, "Corrupt cops deserve to die too!!!"
Once the protesters quieted down, the chief resumed his presentation, promising his department’s full cooperation with the state investigation, according to The Associated Press.
VIDEO SHOWS UNDERCOVER COPS SHOOTING MAN THREATENING SHOPPERS WITH FAKE GUN IN ‘JUSTIFIED’ DEFENSE: OFFICIALS
Officials said a man pulled out a fixed-blade knife and injured an officer in Madison, Wisconsin, on July 22, 2026.  (Madison Police Department)

Court records show Ruiz had a lengthy criminal history spanning nearly three decades. He repeatedly cycled in and out of jail in cases involving failure to pay child support, vehicle theft, bail jumping, threats to authorities, resisting an officer, theft, attempted invasion of privacy and cocaine possession.
Earlier in the briefing, city officials also called for accountability, questioning the circumstances surrounding the shooting.
Madison Mayor Satya Rhodes-Conway said the shooting would be "rigorously investigated" and that no one should lose their life from a law enforcement encounter.
"It does not matter who you are or what your past is, you should not lose your life as a result of an encounter with law enforcement," Rhodes-Conway said, according to the AP.
Madison Common Council President Sabrina Madison went further, questioning why officers involved in fatal shootings should not be taken into custody.
"My first thought is, when the officer’s walking away, why isn’t he walking away in cuffs," Madison said, according to the AP. "I’m angry, there’s no way around it."
Protesters attend a police briefing in Madison, Wisconsin, on July 23, 2026.  (City of Madison)
Gov. Tony Evers also called for transparency and accountability as the investigation moves forward in a statement released Wednesday night.
According to police, Ruiz fled the area on a bicycle and rode through backyards as officers responded to theft reports.
When officers caught up with Ruiz, officials said he "either fell or was pulled off the bicycle," leading to a struggle with officers in the middle of an intersection.
"During the struggle, the man pulled out a fixed-blade knife and injured an officer," the Madison Police Department said.
After unsuccessful attempts to detain Ruiz with a Taser, the officer injured during the encounter reportedly opened fire. Authorities described him as a veteran officer.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A second officer was also injured during the encounter, but it is unclear whether the injury was caused by the knife, according to police.
Officers reportedly attempted to provide life-saving measures at the scene before Ruiz was transported to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
In total, four officers were involved in or witnessed the shooting, and all officers involved will be placed on administrative leave, authorities said.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Witnesses recount 'scary' NYC stabbing after suspect allegedly yelled 'Allahu Akbar' during attacks
summary: A suspect allegedly yelled "Allahu Akbar" before stabbing two men on Manhattan's Upper West Side, with NYPD investigating mental health as a factor.
story: Calvary Chapel Chino Hills senior and founding pastor Jack Hibbs discusses the arrest of a suspect who allegedly yelled ‘Allahu Akbar’ before stabbing two men in New York City on ‘Fox News @ Night.’
Witnesses recounted the moments surrounding a pair of New York City stabbings being investigated as a possible hate crime, with one calling the scene the "scariest thing" she had ever seen.
The suspect, identified as Raul Morales, 51, is accused of yelling "Allahu Akbar" while stabbing two men on Manhattan’s Upper West Side on Thursday afternoon, according to officials.
The NYPD is investigating whether bias played a role in the attacks. One victim is Jewish, while the other is Asian, police said.
Police said the stabbings appeared to be separate attacks that occurred near each other. Authorities said there was no known connection between Morales and either victim or between the two victims.
SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK
The suspect allegedly yelled "Allahu Akbar" during the attack. (Manhattan Shomrim Safety Patrol/@AGHamilton29 via X)
Both men were taken to a hospital in stable condition.
Authorities are investigating whether a knife or screwdriver was used in the attacks.
A witness described seeing a knife sticking out of one of the victims following the stabbing.

"I just saw him sitting on his knees not moving at all, with this knife sticking out. It was the scariest thing I've ever seen. The men who worked in the building are amazing, and they just ran to get help," the witness told Fox 5 New York.

Another woman, who said she was friends with one of the victims, said she was inside a synagogue when she heard that someone had been stabbed. When she reached the scene, the victim was already being taken to the hospital.
The NYPD is looking into the incident as a possible hate crime. (Luiz C. Ribeiro for NY Daily News)

"I spoke to direct eyewitnesses who said that this man had yelled 'Allahu Akbar' and had taken a screwdriver and stabbed him directly in the chest ... then the guy walked away and kind of pretended he was not culpable and said 'maybe someone should call 911, it looks like someone's hurt on the street,'" Nava Silton told the outlet.
Silton said she later visited the victim in the hospital and described him as brave and courageous.
"It is incredibly scary, and he's just praying the condition doesn't get worse. He had to pull the screwdriver out of his body," she said.
Initial NYPD findings suggest mental health may have been a factor.
"While the perpetrator has no known mental health history with the NYPD, the initial investigation suggests that mental health may have been a factor," Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said.
AMERICAN TOURISTS STABBED OUTSIDE ATHENS' ACROPOLIS AS POLICE DETAIN SUSPECT IN APPARENT RANDOM ATTACK
Initial NYPD findings suggest mental health may have been a factor. (Nicolas Economou/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Officials across the state denounced the attack, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Gov. Kathy Hochul.
"These hateful and despicable attacks have no place in our city," Mamdani said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Hochul said she was "disgusted by what appears to be another senseless attack on New Yorkers simply because they’re Jewish."
"Anyone who tries to tear that apart will be met with the full force of the law. New York will stand with our Jewish community today, tomorrow and always," she said.

title: Multiple injured after floatplane makes emergency landing, catches fire off Washington coast
summary: A Kenmore Air seaplane carrying 11 people made an emergency landing near Sucia Island on the Washington coast before catching fire, with one person in critical condition.
story: A small plane made an emergency landing off Honeymoon Island in Florida. Video shows the aircraft partially submerged as everyone onboard safely reached shore, according to reports.
Multiple people were injured Thursday after a Kenmore Air floatplane made an emergency landing off the Washington coast before catching fire, prompting a massive rescue operation, authorities said.

The U.S. Coast Guard said it received a report around 5:25 p.m. local time that a Kenmore Air seaplane had made an emergency landing in North Beach Shallow Bay off Sucia Island before bursting into flames.
Authorities said all 10 passengers and the pilot were accounted for.
SEN TIM SHEEHY MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER IN-FLIGHT ENGINE FAILURE
A Kenmore Air floatplane caught fire after making an emergency landing in North Beach Shallow Bay off Sucia Island, Washington, authorities said. Multiple people were injured. (U.S. Coast Guard)
The San Juan County Sheriff's Office said multiple people suffered injuries ranging from head trauma to broken bones and lacerations.
Kenmore Air said four passengers were taken to local hospitals for treatment. Authorities said one person was in critical condition. No fatalities were immediately reported.
The airline said it was working closely with investigators and would provide additional updates as more information becomes available.
MISSOURI SKYDIVING PLANE CRASH THAT KILLED ALL 12 ABOARD IS A 'DEVASTATING LOSS,' COMPANY SAYS
A Kenmore Air floatplane heads for the dock at the Poulsbo Marina on Tuesday, March 7, 2023. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters)
Kenmore Air CEO David Gudgel said the company's immediate focus was on those aboard the aircraft.
"We are grateful that everyone aboard has been accounted for, and our immediate focus is ensuring our passengers and pilot receive the care and support they need," Gudgel said.

"We extend our sincere thanks to the United States Coast Guard, local emergency responders, and everyone assisting in the response," he continued. "Kenmore Air is fully cooperating with the investigating authorities, and we will continue providing verified information as it becomes available."
The airline said the aircraft involved was a de Havilland DHC-3 Otter operating near Sucia Island.
According to the sheriff's office, the flight departed Seattle's Lake Union and was headed to Roche Harbor Marina on San Juan Island.
A Kenmore Air spokesperson told Fox News Digital the route between Lake Union and the San Juan Islands is a routine flight for the airline.
"If you live here, you would be potentially taking a seaplane up there," the spokesperson said.
COAST GUARD HELICOPTER CRASHES DURING ALASKA TRAINING MISSION, INJURING FOUR CREW MEMBERS
A Kenmore Air pilot pushes his seaplane off the dock after picking up passengers. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)
The sheriff's office said multiple agencies responded by deploying boats and emergency personnel to the scene.
The U.S. Navy also responded, while three air ambulance helicopters transported injured passengers.
Orcas Island Fire & Rescue, Lopez Island Fire & Rescue, San Juan Island Fire & Rescue and San Juan County Parks also responded.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The cause of the accident remains under investigation.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the U.S. Coast Guard for additional comment.

summary: Two people were found with gunshot wounds to the head inside a vehicle near Midway Plaisance Ice Skating Rink on the University of Chicago campus.
story: Harris Faulkner reports on Chicago's escalating violent crime, noting President Trump's repeated offers to deploy the National Guard to Chicago. Illinois Governor JB Pritzker and Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson blast Trump's proposal, arguing he lacks understanding of local safety needs and has defunded institutions that keep people safe in Chicago.

MANHUNT UNDERWAY AFTER COLLEGE STUDENT FATALLY SHOT CHASING ROBBERS WHO ALLEGEDLY STOLE HIS PHONE
The man and the woman both died from a gunshot wound to the head. (iStock)
The man and woman were transported to the university hospital in critical condition, but were later pronounced dead.

It remains unclear if the two victims had any connection to the university. (Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

title: Accused killer's alleged disguises unravel as sheriff releases new clues in month-long manhunt
summary: Walton County Sheriff's Office reveals distinctive tattoos on fugitive Isabelle Johnson as the monthlong manhunt for the murder suspect continues.
story: Criminal defense attorney Donna Rotunno analyzes the manhunt for a woman accused of murdering a 43-year-old man in Florida. Rotunno details how the suspect has allegedly used aliases, altered appearances and manipulation of accomplices to evade the Walton County Sheriff's Department.

A Florida sheriff's office has revealed new identifying marks on a fugitive murder suspect accused in the death of a man found buried in a shallow grave, warning that she may have changed her hair and appearance as a monthlong manhunt continues.
Isabelle Johnson, 38, is wanted in connection with the murder of Jason Coulthart, 43, whose remains were discovered June 25 on a property in Freeport, according to the Walton County Sheriff's Office.
"One month of searching for Isabelle Johnson, and our search has not slowed," the agency wrote in a new appeal for tips.
Investigators now believe Johnson has several distinctive tattoos that could help members of the public recognize her despite any attempts to disguise herself.
FLORIDA WOMAN CHARGED WITH MURDER EVADING POLICE AFTER BODY FOUND IN SHALLOW GRAVE: SHERIFF
Isabelle Johnson, 38, is wanted for the slaying of 43-year-old Jason Christopher Coulthart, the Walton County Sheriff's Office announced. (Walton County Sheriff's Office)

She is believed to have a rose or flower tattoo on her left hand, beginning below the thumb and extending toward the index finger, according to the sheriff's office. She also appears to have an unidentified tattoo on her right ankle and a large scorpion tattoo extending from her left buttock down her left thigh.
Authorities believe Johnson may have dyed and cut her hair in an effort to alter her appearance.
FLORIDA WOMAN ON THE RUN AND WANTED FOR MURDER RELIED ON NETWORK OF ALLEGED ACCOMPLICES TO EVADE CAPTURE: COPS
Isabelle Johnson, 38, was captured on security video days after the remains of Jason Christopher Coulthart, 43, were discovered last month. (Walton County Sheriff's Office)
The sheriff's office once again invoked the aliases Johnson is believed to use.
"Today, we're releasing additional identifying features belonging to Isabelle, or Jessica, or Harley, or whatever name she's going by today," the agency wrote.
Johnson has previously been linked to several aliases, including Harley, Jessica Elaine Bowman, Jessica Elaine Thrush, Jessica Elaine Thrash, Jessica Dowdy and possibly "Denise."
'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN
The Walton County Sheriff’s Office says fugitive Isabelle Johnson has a hand tattoo, an ankle tattoo and a large scorpion tattoo on her left thigh. (Walton County Sheriffs Office)
Authorities say she has ties to Walton and Okaloosa counties in Florida, parts of Georgia and lower Alabama.
Investigators have also warned that she may manipulate people into providing transportation, money or shelter by using stories involving domestic violence or other hardships.
The Walton County Sheriff's Office has described Johnson as "cunning" and a "master manipulator," while urging anyone who may be helping her to stop.
"Every lead is pursued. Every tip is investigated. Every day brings us one step closer," the agency wrote. "Someone knows where she is."
Coulthart was reported missing May 24 after he was last seen leaving the College Condominiums on East College Boulevard in Niceville.

During the missing-person investigation, detectives developed information that led authorities to a property off Sunset Lane in Freeport. Investigators obtained a search warrant and found Coulthart's body buried in a shallow grave that evening, according to the sheriff's office.

Isabelle Rose Johnson, 38, wanted for murder has reportedly been using different disguises to avoid capture by law enforcement. Authorities shared different snapshots of her to ask for the public's help in tracking her down. (Walton County Sheriff's Office)
The District 1 Medical Examiner's Office later identified the remains through DNA testing.

Five people have since been arrested in connection with the case. Michael Ray White, Kathleen Morris, Bobbi Wagstaff, Martin Leaverton and Sandra Leaverton have been charged with accessory to a capital felony after the fact.
Five people have been arrested in connection to the murder of Jason Coulthart. Isabelle Johnson, 38, is still wanted. (Walton County Sheriff's Office)

Authorities previously alleged that White knowingly helped Johnson evade law enforcement, while Morris admitted providing Johnson with transportation and supplies and misleading investigators about whether she had been at her home, according to local reporting.
Walton County Sheriff Michael Adkinson has warned that anyone still helping Johnson hide could also face charges.

"If you give her a place to stay, help her hide, or lie for her, you will face consequences," Adkinson said previously. "This is a homicide case. We will not allow anyone to get in the way of this investigation."
A combined reward of up to $16,000 remains available for information leading to Johnson's arrest.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Walton County Sheriff's Office seeking any additional updates on the investigation.
The sheriff's office ended its latest appeal with a warning aimed at Johnson.

"She can keep running. We won't stop looking," the agency wrote. "We know who will get tired first."
Fox News Digital's Louis Casiano contributed to this report.

title: Foster child allegedly drowned in lake by two teens on local politician’s property: authorities
summary: A 13-year-old foster child was allegedly drowned by two teens at a McCormick County council chairman's home in South Carolina, investigators say.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A temporary foster placement at the home of a South Carolina county council chairman ended in tragedy after investigators say two teens attacked a 13-year-old boy before holding him underwater until he died.
According to The Augusta Press, 13-year-old Daryl Martinez Lowry had only recently been placed in the home of McCormick County Council Chairman Bernie Hamby while awaiting another foster placement.
The outlet reported the two suspects were also foster children living at the home.

One of the teens, Landen Austin Moore, 17, was charged with murder after investigators said he and a 16-year-old got into a physical altercation with Lowry during the early morning hours of July 20, leaving the 13-year-old with knife wounds before the two teens allegedly held him underwater until he died.
TENNESSEE WOMAN ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY TRYING TO DROWN ONE OF HER CHILDREN IN BACKYARD POOL
Daryl Martinez Lowry, 13, was killed July 20 after investigators say two teens attacked him at a boat dock in McCormick County, South Carolina. (Chris King Memorial Chapel)
According to an arrest warrant posted online by the McCormick County Sheriff's Office, the confrontation happened at a private boat dock on Beauregard Drive in Modoc, South Carolina.

The warrant alleges Lowry suffered knife lacerations during the fight before Moore and the unidentified 16-year-old "did unlawfully, intentionally, and with malice aforethought" murder him by "holding him underwater until he became deceased."
MARSHALS NAB TEEN WANTED FOR MURDER OF PENN STATE STUDENT 1,700 MILES FROM CRIME SCENE, 2ND SUSPECT IN CUSTODY
Clarks Hill Lake in South Carolina, where investigators say a 13-year-old boy was held underwater during a deadly attack. (Katie Goodale / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)
The warrant states the allegations are based on witness statements and evidence gathered during the investigation.
The South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) announced Tuesday that Moore was charged with murder after the McCormick County Sheriff's Office requested the state agency investigate the case.
Moore was booked into the McCormick County Detention Center.
MISSING TEEN FOUND HIDING IN CONVICTED SEX OFFENDER'S CLOSET IN FLORIDA, SHERIFF SAYS

Landen Austin Moore, 17, was charged with murder in connection with the death of 13-year-old Daryl Martinez Lowry, according to the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division. (McCormick County Sheriff's Office / Detention Center)

Authorities said the 16-year-old allegedly involved in the incident was transported to the South Carolina Department of Juvenile Justice. SLED has not publicly announced whether that juvenile has been charged.
According to the Augusta Press, Hamby was asleep inside the residence during the alleged attack. Lowry's body was later recovered from the lake.

Authorities have not indicated Hamby witnessed the incident or was involved in the alleged crime. Hamby, a longtime McCormick County councilman who serves as council chairman, has publicly advocated for foster care for years.
Just over a month before his death, Lowry was the subject of a missing child investigation in his hometown of Chester, South Carolina.
Family members described Daryl Martinez Lowry as "full of life, love, and charisma" following his death. (GoFundMe)
On June 12, the Chester Police Department asked for the public's help locating the 13-year-old after he was last seen the previous evening.
"At this time, Daryl's whereabouts are unknown, and we are asking the entire community to remain alert and assist in bringing him home safely," the department wrote in a social media post.
Police urged parents, neighbors and businesses to check surveillance cameras and report "anything suspicious or unusual," adding that officers and investigators were actively pursuing leads.
Later that same day, the department announced Lowry had been found safe.
Authorities have not publicly linked Lowry's earlier disappearance to the circumstances surrounding his death.
A GoFundMe created by Lowry's relatives says the teen had recently been living in a temporary foster home.
"My name is Zyon Simpson, I am the aunt of Daryl Martinez Lowry (13) who was recently murdered while in a temporary foster home," the fundraiser states.
The family described Daryl as "an amazing child full of life, love, and charisma."
"He loved his parents, family, and friends, and he always wore a smile," the fundraiser says.
A woman identifying herself as Lowry's aunt also mourned the 13-year-old in a Facebook post, vowing to seek justice.
"I love you my sweet nephew. We will get justice," she wrote. "You didn't deserve this. No child deserves this... Until we meet again, I will definitely keep your name alive."
Authorities say the fatal confrontation involving three juveniles occurred at a boat dock on Clarks Hill Lake in South Carolina. (Katie Goodale / USA TODAY NETWORK)
McCormick County Sheriff Chad Cox described the killing as an extraordinary tragedy for the rural community while thanking the agencies that helped investigate the case.

"We want to express our deepest condolences to the friends/family of the young man who had his life taken in such a horrendous manner," Cox wrote in a statement posted to the sheriff's office's Facebook page.

Cox thanked SLED, the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources, McCormick County Emergency Services, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the McCormick County Coroner's Office and others who assisted in the investigation.

"We are extremely grateful that we live/work in a community where violent crime is not the regular occurrence," Cox wrote. "But with that being said, no place is exempt from these types of incidents and we must remain diligent in our efforts to keep McCormick County a safe place to live, work and raise families."
SLED said its investigation remains active and ongoing. The case will be prosecuted by the South Carolina Attorney General's Office.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Fox News Digital has reached out to Hamby, the South Carolina Department of Social Services, the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) and the McCormick County Sheriff's Office to independently confirm those details.
Authorities have not accused Hamby of any wrongdoing.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Suspect arrested after allegedly yelling ‘Allahu Akbar,' stabbing 2 men in NYC attack
summary: Suspect Raul Morales is in custody after allegedly yelling "Allahu Akbar" while stabbing two men on Manhattan's Upper West Side in what officials are probing as an antisemitic attack.
story: Two men were stabbed in unprovoked attacks near Central Park by a suspect who allegedly shouted "Allahu Akbar," police said. Investigators are examining possible hate and mental health motives. (Credit: WNYW)

A suspect is in custody after allegedly yelling "Allahu Akbar" while stabbing two men in what officials are describing as an apparent antisemitic attack in Manhattan's Upper West Side Thursday afternoon.

The New York City Police Department (NYPD) said one of the victims is Jewish and that witnesses reported hearing the suspect yell "Allahu Akbar" during both assaults, which took place near West 84th Street and Central Park West, a large Jewish community.
Investigators are evaluating whether the reported attacks should be classified as a hate crime and identified the suspect as Raul Morales, 51, in both assaults.
According to the NYPD, the victims were stabbed in what appeared to be two separate attacks that happened near one another.
NYC ANTISEMITIC INCIDENTS NEARLY TRIPLE DESPITE OTHER CRIMES REACHING RECORD LOWS

Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon shared a photo of the suspect on X. The suspect allegedly yelled "Allahu Akbar" during the attack. (Manhattan Shomrim Safety Patrol/@AGHamilton29 via X)
A 57-year-old man was reportedly attacked near West 84th Street and Central Park West just after 1:30 p.m.
Officials said officers found him conscious and alert with a stab wound to his back. He was taken to a local hospital in stable condition.
Investigators later found a 50-year-old man nearby with a stab wound to his torso. He was also conscious and alert and was taken to a hospital in stable condition.
Initial NYPD findings suggest mental health may have been a factor.
"While the perpetrator has no known mental health history with the NYPD, the initial investigation suggests that mental health may have been a factor," Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said.
WABC reported that police are investigating whether the suspect used a knife or a screwdriver during the alleged attacks.

Hours after the attack, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who recently called on the federal government to arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, said he had been briefed on what he described as "horrifying stabbings" and noted the victims were an Asian man and a Jewish man.

"According to witness and victim statements, the perpetrator yelled 'Allahu Akbar' during both attacks," Mamdani said. "The NYPD responded immediately and arrested Raul Morales in connection with both assaults — and I am grateful to the officers for their swift response."
Mamdani issued his statement roughly two hours after City Council Speaker Julie Menin and about 45 minutes after Gov. Kathy Hochul.
CALLS FOR US TO DO MORE AS ANTISEMITIC ACTS SKYROCKET IN EUROPE: 'ENORMOUSLY PAINFUL'
An Israeli flag is fixed to a street sign as police stand by June 1, 2025. (Eli Imadali/AFP via Getty Images)
"I am absolutely sickened and furious by what appears to be an antisemitic stabbing on the Upper West Side," Menin wrote in a post on X.

"While we await additional details to be confirmed, we know that what is happening in our city is abhorrent," Menin said. "The fear in the Jewish community is real. Every New Yorker deserves to feel safe in their neighborhood, regardless of their faith or identity.
"We must remain united in condemning antisemitism and ensuring those responsible are held fully accountable," she added. "I thank the NYPD for its swift response in apprehending the assailant."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
New York Assembly member Micah Lasher, a Jewish representative of the area, said he was also in contact with investigators.

"I am in touch with the NYPD and community leaders about the stabbing of two individuals on the Upper West Side today," Lasher said. "The NYPD responded immediately and has apprehended a suspect. I am praying for the survival and recovery of the victims and will provide more information as I have it."
Hochul posted on X, saying she is "disgusted by what appears to be another senseless attack on New Yorkers simply because they’re Jewish."

"The strength of New York has always been our ability to live together across every faith and background," Hochul added. "Anyone who tries to tear that apart will be met with the full force of the law. New York will stand with our Jewish community today, tomorrow, and always."
Minister of Foreign Affairs of the State of Israel Gideon Sa'ar added he was "appalled but sadly not surprised" by the incident, blaming Mamdani for creating "a climate in which Jews are targeted."
"I am appalled by the horrific antisemitic stabbing attack in New York. Appalled but sadly not surprised," he said in a post on X.

"This violence did not happen in a vacuum. Months of incitement against the Jewish state from Mamdani have helped create a climate in which Jews are targeted. Words have consequences. Mamdani must end the incitement, confront antisemitism with resolve, and act now to protect the city’s Jewish community."
Mamdani's office, along with the FBI, did not immediately respond to further inquiries from Fox News Digital.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: ICC prosecutor whose Netanyahu warrant fueled Mamdani arrest threat is fired over sexual misconduct
summary: ICC member states voted to remove chief prosecutor Karim Khan over sexual misconduct allegations, marking the first such dismissal in the court's history. His lawyer says he will appeal decision.
story: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani acknowledges he lacks independent legal authority to enforce an International Criminal Court arrest warrant against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.  The discussion highlights the mayor's focus on international issues over local governance.

The International Criminal Court prosecutor whose arrest warrant against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu became central to New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s threat to arrest the Israeli leader was dismissed Friday after member states voted to remove him over sexual misconduct allegations.

Karim Khan, the ICC’s chief prosecutor, was removed after a vote by the Assembly of States Parties, the court’s 125-member governing body, following disciplinary proceedings tied to allegations involving a junior female staffer in his office. Khan has denied wrongdoing.

The decision marked the first time in the ICC’s history that a sitting chief prosecutor has been removed from office. Khan’s removal comes days after Secretary of State Marco Rubio launched a U.S. campaign to "dismantle" the ICC, accusing the court of threatening American sovereignty.
MAMDANI GOES BACK ON CAMPAIGN PROMISE, SAYS NYC CAN'T ARREST NETANYAHU
Karim Khan is the ICC's chief prosecutor. (Getty Images)

Khan became one of the world’s most controversial prosecutors after pursuing ICC arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant over Israel’s war against Hamas in Gaza. The ICC issued the warrants in November 2024, prompting fierce condemnation from Israel and the United States, neither of which is a member of the court.

The warrants also became a flashpoint in New York politics after Mamdani repeatedly invoked the ICC case against Netanyahu. Mamdani said during his campaign that he would seek to arrest Netanyahu if the Israeli prime minister came to New York, and later acknowledged as mayor that the city lacks authority to enforce the warrant while calling on the federal government to do so.

The ICC, based in The Hague in Holland, is a permanent international court created under the Rome Statute to prosecute individuals accused of genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and the crime of aggression when national courts are unable or unwilling to act.
WORLD COURT PROSECUTOR WHO WENT AFTER NETANYAHU FOR WAR CRIMES SUSPENDED OVER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT
A general view of the International Criminal Court (ICC) building in The Hague, Netherlands on April 30, 2024. ((Photo by Selman Aksunger/Anadolu via Getty Images))

The allegations against Khan have triggered a crisis for the court. Reuters reported that 82 of the ICC’s 125 member states voted in favor of his removal, exceeding the absolute majority required. Khan had previously stepped aside in May 2025 while a U.N. oversight investigation was underway and was suspended in June 2026 pending the final vote.

The Associated Press reported that the court’s oversight body found Khan had committed "serious misconduct." The case involved allegations from a female aide who said Khan engaged in nonconsensual sexual conduct. Khan’s lawyers have denied the allegations and called the removal process legally flawed and unsupported by evidence.
The woman, identified only as Sarah, went public in a CNN interview last week. "There is no way for something to be consensual when you have such a power disparity," she told CNN.

Khan’s legal team rejected the vote and said he would challenge the decision. Tayab Ali, partner at Bindmans LLP and head of Khan’s legal team, said in a statement that the Assembly of States Parties had disregarded due process concerns raised publicly by more than 180 nongovernmental organizations and senior international lawyers.

"The decision is unsupported by any lawful or properly reasoned finding that Mr Khan KC committed misconduct or breached his duties as Prosecutor," Ali said. "He has denied the allegations from the outset and continues to do so." Ali said the allegations were investigated for more than a year by the U.N. Office of Internal Oversight Services and argued that "there is not a single finding of misconduct, including sexual misconduct, anywhere in the OIOS report." He also said a three-judge panel unanimously determined in March 2026 that the factual findings made by OIOS did not establish misconduct or breach of duty by Khan.

International Criminal Court Prosecutor Karim Khan poses during an interview with AFP at the Cour d'Honneur of the Palais Royal in Paris on February 7, 2024. The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) wants to prosecute "environmental crimes" without changing the court's statute, because environmental damage is often the cause or consequence of war crimes or crimes against humanity that the ICC can already judge, Karim Khan announced on February 7, 2024, in an interview with AFP. Dimitar Dilkoff/AFP via Getty Images (Dimitar Dilkoff/AFP via Getty Images)

Khan’s lawyers accused the Assembly of States Parties of removing him through a politically driven and procedurally unfair process, saying Khan and his lawyers were not allowed to make formal submissions to the Assembly before the vote.

"The Prosecutor of this Court has been removed by an executive vote while under sanctions and while the Court is under immense political pressure," Ali said.Ali said Khan "will challenge the lawfulness and fairness of the decision through all available legal mechanisms."
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a still image taken from handout video released on July 21, 2026. (Reuters)
Israeli officials argued Friday that Khan’s removal undermined the legitimacy of the ICC’s actions against Netanyahu.

Israeli Ambassador to the United Nations Danny Danon told Fox News Digital that Khan believed "by launching a political witch hunt against Israel and issuing a politically-motivated arrest warrant against Prime Minister Netanyahu, the world would ignore the grave sexual misconduct allegations against him."
"He was wrong," Danon said. "He sought to scapegoat Israel in an attempt to divert attention from his own misconduct. The international community rejected that cynical attempt today."
NETANYAHU FIRES BACK AT NYC MAYOR MAMDANI'S VOW TO ENFORCE 'BOGUS ARREST WARRANT'
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (left) and ICC chief prosecutor Karim Khan (right).
Danon added, "The attacks against Israel, which were intended to distract from his disgraceful conduct, did not save Karim Khan, and they will not help Zohran Mamdani either."

Anne Bayefsky, president of Human Rights Voices and director of the Touro Institute on Human Rights and the Holocaust, told Fox News Digital that Khan’s fall should not be viewed as an isolated scandal. "He unexpectedly requested arrest warrants for Israel’s prime minister and defense minister within weeks of discovering his sexual deviancy had been revealed. He accused his victim of being a Mossad agent. He and his lawyers constantly repeated the refrain that Israelis were behind the accusations."

Bayefsky claimed that Khan’s conduct has damaged the ICC itself. "Now there is a massive campaign to save the ICC from Khan. On this logic, Khan’s anti-Israel fanaticism never tainted his investigation of Israel, his arrest warrant request against Israelis, his submissions to the ICC Court, the evidence he placed before the Court, or the analysis and conclusions of the ICC Court that placed their trust in him when they decided to grant his warrant requests."
Israel's U.N. Ambassador Danny Danon speaking at the General Assembly. (U.N. Photo/ Eskinder Debebe)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The ICC has not said Khan’s removal affects the Netanyahu and Gallant warrants, which were issued by judges after Khan’s request.
Requests sent to Khan's office for comment were not answered by the time of publication.

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is an investigative journalist, filmmaker and war correspondent. She has directed and produced over 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries. Recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award, Lachter is also a 2023-24 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Romanian F-16 shoots down drone after airspace breach, marking first for NATO ally
summary: A Romanian F-16 shot down an unauthorized drone over Buzău County, marking the first such interception in the NATO member's national airspace.
story: Russian officials say two people were wounded and buildings caught fire after one of the largest drone attacks on the Moscow region. (Reuters)

A Romanian F-16 fighter jet shot down a drone that entered the country’s airspace without authorization Friday, marking the first time the NATO member has intercepted and destroyed a drone inside its national airspace, authorities said.

Romanian officials have not yet identified the drone’s origin or purpose. Romania’s army chief said pilots described it as appearing to be a Shahed-type drone, Reuters reported, the Iran-designed attack drone widely used by Russia against Ukraine.

The incident carries direct implications for the U.S. and its NATO allies, as repeated airspace breaches along the alliance’s eastern flank have fueled concerns that Russia’s war in Ukraine could spill across NATO borders. Romania, which borders Ukraine, has reported dozens of drone incursions or debris incidents since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.
Romanian Foreign Minister Oana Țoiu said the interception took place over an unpopulated area in Buzău County.
REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES
An F-16 fighter jet takes part in the NATO Air Shielding exercise near the air base in Lask, central Poland, Oct. 12, 2022. (Radoslaw Jozwiak/AFP via Getty Images)

"Our borders and our sovereignty are non-negotiable, and our military and NATO air police will continue to monitor the land border, the Danube and the Black Sea, as our military frequently identifies risks," Țoiu told Fox News Digital.

"The impact area and the drone debris are currently being analyzed, but the pattern is consistent with prior confirmed Russian drone flights during the numerous illegal attacks against Ukrainian civilian infrastructure on Romania’s border," she added.
Țoiu said Romania and NATO would continue to defend allied territory.

"NATO works, and we plan to be even stronger with the decisions on air defense and budget allocation from The Hague and Ankara summits," she said. "The path toward increased security is the path toward peace at Romania’s border. We will defend our citizens and we will continue to invest in protecting Romanian and Allied territory."
THE TWO MOST IMPORTANT AMERICAN WEAPONS SYSTEMS NATO IS EAGER TO HAVE

Explosion following what Romania's defense ministry says was a detonation of Russian drone fragments found in a location given as near Rachelu village, Romania, in this screengrab taken from a handout video released June 30, 2026. (Romanian Defence Ministry/Handout via Reuters)

Țoiu previously told Fox News Digital July 2 that Russian drones had been detected inside Ukraine roughly 19 miles from Romania’s border, prompting two Royal Air Force Eurofighter Typhoon jets operating from Romania’s 86th Air Base in Fetești to scramble under NATO’s Enhanced Air Policing mission. A Romanian Air Force IAR 330 Puma helicopter was also deployed, she said at the time.

Romanian President Nicușor Dan and Defense Minister Radu Miruță reaffirmed the country’s commitment to protecting its airspace and investing in modern air-defense and anti-drone capabilities, according to Țoiu.

The incident underscores the growing danger along NATO’s eastern flank as Russia continues strikes across Ukraine and Kyiv increasingly targets Russian military and energy infrastructure deeper inside Russia.
RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY

Emergency employees work at the site of a Russian missile strikes, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv region, July 24, 2026. (Press service of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine/Handout via Reuters)
The drone shootdown came as Ukraine reported deadly Russian strikes in the Kyiv region and Slovyansk.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a rescue operation was underway in the Kyiv region after a Russian missile strike killed six people and wounded dozens. Reuters later reported that Ukrainian officials and industry representatives said the strike killed 10 people and injured close to 100 at a site where a defense industry event was being held.

"There were also casualties in Slovyansk following guided aerial bomb strikes," Zelenskyy said. "Five people were killed. My condolences to their families. Nine others were injured. The Russians damaged ordinary homes, the consulate building, and vehicles."

Latvian Foreign Minister Baiba Braže said Latvia’s honorary consulate building in Slovyansk, in Ukraine’s Donetsk Oblast, was destroyed Friday morning in a Russian attack involving a KAB-250 guided aerial bomb, according to information provided by Ukrainian authorities.

Braže said Latvia’s honorary consul, Oleksandr Pavenko, was not injured, but two consulate staff members were wounded. She informed European Union and NATO foreign ministers and international organizations about the incident, while Latvia summoned Russia’s chargé d’affaires and delivered a note of protest.

"Russia will be held accountable for this and other violations of international law," Latvia’s Foreign Ministry said. "All war crimes committed by Russia must be thoroughly investigated, and those responsible must be brought to justice."
Zelenskyy called the strikes "brutal attacks on civilians" and again pressed Ukraine’s partners for air-defense support.
"Interceptors for Patriot systems are the number one priority," he said.

Ukraine also said its forces had struck one of Russia’s key military enterprises in Kirov, which Zelenskyy said supplies components for Russian aircraft and missile systems used in attacks on Ukrainian cities. Zelenskyy said Ukraine had also hit an oil facility nearly 840 miles away and that operations against Russian logistics supplying drone components, navigation equipment and military gear remained underway. Ukrainian outlet UNN reported that Zelenskyy confirmed the Kirov strike and the long-range strike on the oil facility.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Smoke rises from Wildberries facility, from what the Ukrainian authorities say was following a drone attack, in Shushary, Pushkinsky District, St. Petersburg, Russia July 24, 2026 in this screen grab taken from a social media video. (Social media/via Reuters)

The Security Council is expected to hold an emergency meeting on Ukraine Monday at 10 a.m., as requested by Ukraine, according to a United Nations schedule viewed by Fox News Digital. The meeting comes after Kyiv has repeatedly urged the international community to respond more forcefully to Russia’s attacks on civilians and infrastructure.
The back-and-forth comes as Kyiv is trying to show battlefield momentum despite continued Russian missile and drone attacks.

Outgoing Ukrainian Commander in Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi said Ukraine had recaptured 270 square miles of territory in 2026 and was handing over to his successor "an army that is not only holding the defence but is also on the offensive," Reuters reported Wednesday.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Russian defense ministry but didn't receive a response in time for publication.
Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Could this African nation become Trump's next terror target as jihadists close in on power?
summary: Mali's gold and lithium deposits add a minerals dimension as Trump's team reportedly weighs strikes against al Qaeda-linked terrorists in the Sahel.
story: Africa Command Gen. Dagvin Anderson tells lawmakers that shrinking U.S. presence in Africa has weakened intelligence capabilities as Russia, China and terrorist groups expand influence across the continent.
JOHANNESBURG: The U.S. is reportedly considering airstrikes against al Qaeda-linked terrorists in Mali, according to regional analysts and recent media reports.

The military junta that has been running this West African country in the Sahel region since coups in both 2020 and 2021 turned away from France and the U.S. to get military protection from Russia and its Africa Corps mercenaries against jihadist groups.

But now the largest of these groups, Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), which has Mali’s capital under siege, is credited, along with another group, for killing 50 Malian soldiers this month, for the death of the country’s defense minister earlier this year and has reportedly sent battalions of Russian soldiers retreating on at least two occasions this year.
ISIS POISED TO EXPLOIT HISTORIC US IRAQ EXIT, TERROR GROUP 'ACTIVELY WAITING IN THE GAPS,' EXPERT WARNS
Malian troops parade during the country's 65th anniversary of the African nation's independence. (Habib Kouyate/Xinhua via Getty Images)

JNIM is said to want to change the country into an Islamist Jihadist state. If they succeed, Mali would be the first country in the world to be run by a jihadist group. The organization was designated officially as a Foreign Terrorist Organization during the first Trump administration in 2018.
Islamic State (ISIS) jihadist groups are also operating freely in Mali, and are linked to terror groups in neighboring Nigeria.

A State Department official didn’t respond to a Washington Post report that the U.S. is considering strikes against JNIM in Mali, but used strong language Thursday when talking to Fox News Digital, leading analysts to suggest the time for talking may be over.

"The United States unequivocally condemns the terrorist activity in Mali," the official said, adding, "in the Sahel, the United States is committed to promoting regional ownership and cooperation against terrorist threats, and monitoring indicators and warnings of threats to our homeland."

This undated photograph handed out by the French military shows three Russian mercenaries, right, in northern Mali. Russia has engaged in under-the-radar military operations in at least half a dozen countries in Africa in the last five years using a shadowy mercenary force analysts say is loyal to President Vladimir Putin. The analysts say the Wagner Group of mercenaries is also key to Putin's ambitions to re-impose Russian influence on a global scale. (French Army via AP)

Edmund Fitton-Brown, a former British and United Nations diplomat, said the U.S. could order military action, to primarily try and stop jihadists becoming entrenched in Mali. Fitton-Brown, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital, "Mali is mainly important to the U.S. because, as a failed state becoming a safe haven for al Qaeda and ISIS, it looks like the first of several African dominoes likely to fall."

Retired U.S. Air Force Maj. Gen. Kenneth P. Ekman, who until last year, served as the Department of War’s West Africa Coordination Element lead, said that with strike action the administration may be able to persuade Mali’s rulers to turn away from Russia, and towards the U.S. for protection – and purchases of military equipment.
RESOURCE-RICH NATION PRAISES US TIES AMID WASHINGTON-BEIJING CRITICAL MINERALS RACE

A column of black smoke rises above buildings as traffic passes the Africa Tower monument in Bamako on April 26, 2026. April 25, 2026's shock attacks, synchronized by Tuareg rebels of the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) coalition and the jihadist Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM), targeted several areas in the vast arid country. Fighting resumed on April 26 in several areas, including Kita near Bamako, Kidal, Gao and Severe.Tuareg rebels meanwhile announced an agreement allowing Russian forces backing Mali's army to withdraw from the northern city of Kidal, which they claimed was "totally" under their control. (AFP via Getty Images)

Ekman told Fox News Digital, "JNIM has a stranglehold on the government and much of the population. The Russians are woefully ineffective and extractive. Cooperation with U.S. forces offers a disproportionate and positive impact."

Ekman said that U.S. forces have supported partner-led operations against JNIM before, as recently as 2022, adding "⁠recent proposals amount to returning to similar cooperation against a mutual threat."

The administration may also be in a minerals frame of mind. Mali is one of Africa’s largest gold-producing nations. It also has substantial deposits of lithium, used extensively in rechargeable batteries.
Fitton-Brown said that "President Trump may be less reluctant than his predecessor to work with the juntas in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, if they are losing faith in their Russian friends."
A vehicle turned up following a brutal ambush on Russian Wagner fighters in Mali on July 27, 2024. (East2West)

He continued, "The U.S. is certainly a more capable partner. France has already been displaced, so all three countries might accept U.S. help if it comes only with strings attached that don’t offend or disadvantage them. Whether even the U.S. is capable of stopping the political decline of these countries, and the rise of militant Islam, is another matter. That cannot be achieved by military force alone."

The FDD’s Fitton-Brown said U.S. assets such as aircraft may not be directly involved if there is a strike, "The U.S. might work with French and other intelligence services to develop local intelligence for strikes on JNIM leadership, but this is unlikely to achieve much. The organization is resilient and will be able to replace those killed."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

A former senior Department of War official told Fox News Digital the U.S. has at its disposal cruise missiles and long-range bombers. Attack drones would probably not come into play, and the U.S. Naval Institute’s Fleet Tracker shows no American aircraft carriers anywhere near African waters, effectively ruling out carrier operations.
However, Ekman believes airstrikes are under consideration, noting "JNIM and ISIS are a threat to U.S. interests, and are ascendant in West Africa."
Paul Tilsley is a veteran correspondent who has reported from four continents for more than three decades. Based in Johannesburg, South Africa, he can be followed on X @paultilsley.

title: Is Israel really isolated? Polls and diplomacy point in opposite directions
summary: Trump says the Saudi Arabia nuclear deal hinges on joining the Abraham Accords, as experts debate whether Israel faces isolation or expanding ties.
story: Richard Goldberg argues that Israel’s strategic relationships are expanding even as opposition grows among Democrats, international institutions and parts of Western public opinion.

President Donald Trump predicted in recent days that additional countries would soon join the Abraham Accords, renewing debate over whether Israel is becoming increasingly isolated or continuing to expand its most important strategic relationships.

"The Abraham Accords have been, I think, a tremendous success," Trump said during a Tuesday Oval Office meeting with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun. "I think you’re going to see a lot of countries joining pretty soon."

Trump's prediction underscores a central debate about Israel's global position: Public support for the country has fallen sharply in the United States and across much of the world, yet Israel continues to build or preserve diplomatic, military, energy and technology relationships with foreign governments.
TRUMP CALLS ON ARAB NATIONS TO SIGN ABRAHAM ACCORDS
President Donald Trump predicted in recent days that additional countries would soon join the Abraham Accords. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

The Abraham Accords, brokered by the Trump administration in 2020, normalized relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco and Sudan. Trump has made expanding the agreements a central goal of his Middle East strategy.

The dispute depends partly on how isolation is measured. Critics point to worsening public opinion, pressure at international institutions and growing opposition among Democrats and younger voters. Israeli officials and conservative foreign-policy experts argue that government-to-government cooperation remains strong and, in some regions, is expanding.

Trump reinforced that strategy Thursday by saying a U.S. civilian nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia would depend on the kingdom joining the Abraham Accords. The statement showed the administration attempting to use one of Washington’s most valuable offers to Riyadh to secure normalization with Israel, but it did not demonstrate that Saudi Arabia had agreed to do so.
Israeli Ambassador to the United Nations Danny Danon rejected the contention that Israel had become isolated.

"The claim that Israel is an isolated country is simply not true," Danon told Fox News Digital. "While the campaign to dismantle the Hamas terrorist organization has drawn international criticism, Israel’s relationships with other countries have not weakened. They have evolved."

Former White House national security official Richard Goldberg similarly argued that Israel retains strong support among conservatives and that its electoral gains are translating into closer government relations.

"Polling in the United States shows massive support among conservatives and Republicans, including self-described MAGA, for Israel still," Goldberg told Fox News Digital. "And that’s reflected around the world, particularly among conservative candidates and parties that win elected office right now."

Goldberg pointed to political changes in Latin America, expanding partnerships in the Eastern Mediterranean and Israel’s continuing defense and technology relationships as evidence that public criticism has not translated into comprehensive strategic isolation.
The dispute comes amid polling that shows Israel retaining deep support among Republicans while losing ground across the broader American electorate and much of the world.
POTENTIAL 2028 DEM CONTENDER UNLOADS ON NETANYAHU, ADMITS US-ISRAEL TIES AT 'CROSSROADS'
Anti-Israel protests in Istanbul. (Bulent Kilic/AFP via Getty Images)

Eighty percent of self-identified MAGA Republicans said Israel’s security matters to U.S. security and prosperity, a Reagan Institute survey released in June found, while 73% supported sending Israel U.S. weapons. Among MAGA Republicans under 30, 63% said Israel’s security matters to the United States and 60% supported sending weapons.

The same survey found that broader support was narrowing. Sixty-five percent of Americans said Israel’s security matters to U.S. security and prosperity, down six percentage points from a year earlier.
The figure fell nine points among Democrats to 57%, compared with 75% of Republicans and 80% of MAGA Republicans.

A Pew Research Center survey published in June found that a median of 67% of adults across 36 countries viewed Israel unfavorably, while 25% viewed it favorably. The findings came from Pew’s Spring 2026 Global Attitudes Survey.

In the United States, 60% of adults viewed Israel unfavorably, up from 53% in 2025 and 42% in 2022, according to a separate Pew survey conducted March 23 to March 29. Eighty percent of Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents held an unfavorable view, while negative assessments were also widespread among adults under 50.

Israel no longer held a statistically significant advantage over the Palestinians in Americans’ sympathies, Gallup reported in February. Forty-one percent said they sympathized more with the Palestinians and 36% with the Israelis, although Gallup said the five-point difference was not statistically significant.
In 2023, 54% sympathized more with Israelis and 31% with Palestinians.
Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel highlighted that erosion during a July 8 speech at Tel Aviv University.
"Support for Israel around the world is declining," Emanuel said, "The only diplomatic achievement Israel has secured in the past three years is Somaliland."
THE US-ISRAEL STRATEGIC ALLIANCE – PARTNERSHIP, NOT CHARITY
Anti-Israel activists hold banners that include, "globalize the intifada" during a protest commemorating Nakba Day May 15, 2025, in Brooklyn, New York. (Alexi Rosenfeld/Getty Images)

Emanuel’s conclusion focuses on Israel’s declining public legitimacy and its strained position in traditional diplomatic institutions. Goldberg and Danon argue that it overlooks expanding government-to-government relationships built around defense, intelligence, energy, technology and trade.
Goldberg pointed in particular to Latin America, where he said newly elected conservative governments have made closer ties with Israel an early priority.

"Every time a government in South America right now flips from left wing to right wing, one of the first things they do is reestablish better relations with Israel, withdraw recognition of a Palestinian state and see what else they can do to make Israel a strategic partner," Goldberg said.
He cited Argentina under President Javier Milei and the proposed "Isaac Accords," along with political changes in Chile, Colombia and Bolivia, as evidence of a broader realignment.
Goldberg also argued that Israel remains central to emerging partnerships involving energy, defense, intelligence and critical infrastructure.

"If you’re in the Eastern Mediterranean and you’re Greece and you are Cyprus, you’re thinking about how do we work with Israel to make the Eastern Mediterranean partnership even stronger," he said. "If you’re Armenia and Azerbaijan in a tough neighborhood between Turkey and Iran, you’re talking to Israel, you’re getting closer to Israel."

Israel, Greece and Cyprus reaffirmed their strategic partnership during a trilateral summit in December 2025, agreeing to expand cooperation in energy, security, emergency preparedness and regional connectivity.
Danon said the diplomatic shift is visible even inside the United Nations, an institution where Israel routinely faces critical resolutions and public condemnation.

"We see this every day in the corridors of the United Nations," he said. "While many South American countries were once highly critical of Israel in recent years, we are now cooperating with many of them. These discussions are happening in public and behind the scenes."

"As Israel’s official representative to the United Nations, I regularly meet with ambassadors from around the world, including from Arab countries, to quietly advance initiatives where we share common interests," Danon said.
Danon went further than Goldberg in assessing Israel’s position since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attacks and the subsequent war.

"Compared to the period before October 7, Israel is in a far stronger geostrategic position," Danon said. "That is reflected not only in regional developments but also in the country’s diplomatic relationships around the world."
The competing evidence suggests that much of the disagreement depends on how isolation is defined.

Israel may be losing public support and influence in traditional international institutions while simultaneously preserving or expanding government-to-government cooperation in defense, technology, intelligence, energy and agriculture.
MAMDANI GOES BACK ON CAMPAIGN PROMISE, SAYS NYC CAN’T ARREST NETANYAHU

European Union Council President, Charles Michel (center), Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic (right) and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (left) meet in January 2020 in West Jerusalem. (PhKobi Gideon / GPO / Handout/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images)
Goldberg acknowledged that relationships driven by conservative political victories could become vulnerable when governments change.
But he argued that Israel is increasingly building relationships around durable national interests rather than political ideology alone.

The central risk for Israel is that today’s collapse in public opinion could eventually reshape tomorrow’s government policies. Conservative governments may currently protect and expand strategic ties, but younger voters and left-wing parties could alter those relationships after future elections.
Israel is scheduled to hold national elections Oct. 27, the country’s first since the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks.
Goldberg argued that a change in Israel’s government would provide a test of whether international opposition is directed primarily at Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or at Israel itself.

"If there is somebody else who becomes prime minister next, we will have to evaluate," Goldberg said. "Those very loud detractors of Israel who right now use Netanyahu as their symbol for bashing and say it’s not about Israel, it’s about Netanyahu, they’ll be put to the test very quickly."
He noted that the boycott movement and anti-Israel campus organizations remained active during the previous government led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, when Netanyahu was not prime minister.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

President Donald Trump predicted in recent days that additional countries would soon join the Abraham Accords, renewing debate over whether Israel is becoming increasingly isolated or continuing to expand its most important strategic relationships. (Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)
"Is their hatred and venom really just about Bibi Netanyahu, or is it fundamentally about a Jewish state that they don’t like existing?" Goldberg asked.

For now, both realities appear to be unfolding at once: Israel remains a sought-after military, intelligence and technology partner for a growing group of governments, while its support among the global public has fallen to levels that could eventually threaten those relationships.

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is an investigative journalist, filmmaker and war correspondent. She has directed and produced over 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries. Recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award, Lachter is also a 2023-24 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: French modeling scout linked to Jeffrey Epstein found dead in Paris apartment
summary: Daniel Siad's name appeared roughly 2,000 times in the Epstein files, and at least 24 women came forward as alleged victims or witnesses in a trafficking probe.
story: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche pushed back July 15, 2026, on claims the DOJ has closed the book on Jeffrey Epstein's crimes, saying prosecutors are ready to pursue anyone criminally linked to the late financier's trafficking operation.
A French modeling scout with ties to Jeffrey Epstein was found dead inside his Paris apartment, prosecutors said.
The body of Daniel Siad, 69, was discovered Monday night, and an autopsy is pending. Siad's attorney, Menya Arab-Tigrine, told Fox News Digital he died of a heart attack.

"While he died of a heart attack, the unbearable waiting, the stigma cast upon him and, by extension, his loved ones as well as the daily pressure and anxiety he endured, undoubtedly played a role," she said. "We must await the autopsy results to determine whether his body simply gave out."
Fox News Digital has reached out to French prosecutors.
JEFFREY EPSTEIN'S PURPORTED SUICIDE NOTE UNSEALED BY FEDERAL JUDGE IN CELLMATE'S CASE
Daniel Siad, 69, a French modeling scout with ties to Jeffrey Epstein, was found dead inside his Paris apartment, prosecutors said Wednesday. (Justice Department)
Siad's name appeared about 2,000 times in the Epstein files released by the Justice Department, Reuters reported.
"I am here in Barcelona I have girls staying with me from Australia Croecian origin, so you can speak with her very Sweet," Siad allegedly wrote to Epstein in one email.
"I am looking to place her here and Paris."
DEMOCRAT CALLS HOWARD LUTNICK A 'PATHOLOGICAL LIAR' AFTER CLOSED-DOOR EPSTEIN TESTIMONY

This photograph taken July 22, 2026, shows the home of model agent Daniel Siad in Colombes, a north-western suburb of Paris, where he was found dead July 20. Authorities opened an investigation into the cause of death and ordered a postmortem examination. (AFP via Getty Images)
"Photo?" Epstein replied.
Another email from Siad to Epstein from April 2009 included images of a 17-year-old Slovakian girl while he was scouting models in Bratislava.

At least 24 women have come forward as victims or witnesses of alleged acts committed by Siad or others after the February launch of a human trafficking and fraud probe, Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau told Reuters.
Jeffrey Epstein was found dead in federal custody in 2019. (New York State Sex Offender Registry via AP, File)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Investigators looked into Siad, but there wasn't enough evidence to justify his immediate arrest, said Arab-Tigrine.

"Let us not forget that he was never prosecuted, nor was he ever formally implicated in any legal proceedings," she said. "In the coming days, we must respect the grief of his loved ones. He has passed away, and he was innocent."
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Nicaragua's parliament plans to eliminate elections to codify President Ortega's declaration
summary: Nicaragua's congress moves to abolish elections after President Daniel Ortega declared no more elections, drawing condemnation from the international community.
story: Sen. Ron Johnson responds to New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill's admission of 6,600 non-citizens improperly registered to vote due to a software error, with 400 actually voting. Johnson, from Wisconsin, stresses that election integrity, including voter ID and cleaning voter rolls, should be a non-partisan issue to restore public confidence in U.S. elections.

Nicaragua's lawmakers announced plans to abolish elections in the Central American country, following through on President Daniel Ortega's declaration over the weekend that there would be no more elections, which enraged the international community.

The move was revealed on Tuesday by Nicaragua's congress, which is firmly in the hands of Ortega and his wife, Rosario Murillo. Lawmakers said the planned constitutional overhaul will ensure Nicaragua's "peace, security and stability."

With the announcement, lawmakers are making good on Ortega's promise of no more elections, further closing off any potential path for the opposition to challenge the government he leads with Murillo, whom constitutional reforms elevated from vice president to "co-president."

"There won't be any more elections here for them to try to seize the government and seize power," Ortega said on Sunday during a speech commemorating the 1979 Sandinista revolution, in which Ortega participated in the overthrow of the U.S.-backed dictatorship of Anastasio Somoza.
NICARAGUA'S ORTEGA SAYS COUNTRY WILL 'NEVER AGAIN' HOLD ELECTIONS, SHUTTING OUT OPPOSITION
Nicaragua's President Daniel Ortega said officials in the Central American country will no longer hold elections. (Reuters/Leonardo Fernandez Viloria)
"The days when parties backed by the Yankees (United States) and the Somocistas would return to power are over — never again," he declared.
The declaration appeared to eliminate the possibility of a future electoral challenge as Ortega and Murillo continue consolidating control over the country’s political institutions.

Ortega and Murillo expanded their authority through sweeping constitutional changes that took effect in 2025. The reforms included extending the presidential term from five years to six and placing the legislative, judicial and electoral institutions under the authority of the presidency.
The pair now exercise control over nearly every branch of government, including the armed forces, police and judiciary.

Ortega, Nicaragua’s longest-serving leader, is scheduled to remain in office until early 2028, although his statement on Sunday effectively canceled Nicaragua’s next elections, which had been scheduled for November 2027.
Critics say Ortega had already effectively eliminated meaningful electoral competition during elections in 2011, 2016 and 2021.
REPUBLICAN REP MARÍA ELVIRA SALAZAR DECLARES, 'AFTER CUBA, NICARAGUA IS NEXT'
President Daniel Ortega's promise to abolish elections prompted widespread condemnation from the international community. (Carlos Becerra/Bloomberg)

Many prominent opposition leaders have been imprisoned, forced into exile or stripped of their Nicaraguan citizenship, while opposition parties and independent civic organizations have lost their legal status.

A United Nations group of experts has accused the Ortega-Murillo government of systematically violating human rights as part of a campaign to eliminate criticism and preserve its hold on power. The experts said some alleged violations may amount to crimes against humanity.
The government launched a violent crackdown on anti-government protests in 2018. More than 300 people were killed during the unrest, according to international human rights groups.
Ortega's effort to abolish elections prompted widespread condemnation from foreign governments, including the U.S.

"Daniel Ortega’s declaration that, under his family’s dictatorship, Nicaragua will never again hold elections lays bare their true authoritarian nature. Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo have abandoned even the pretense of popular consent," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday.

"The Nicaraguan people have the right to choose their own leaders through democratic elections. The United States calls on the international community to join forces to demonstrate to the Murillo-Ortega dictatorship that it cannot expect to maintain business as usual with other nations when it is thwarting the basic tenets of our democratic hemisphere," he added.
The move to abolish elections was announced by Nicaragua's congress, which is firmly in the hands of President Daniel Ortega and his wife, Rosario Murillo. (INTI OCON/AFP)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The Trump administration has described the Ortega-Murillo government as a dictatorship and imposed sanctions on members of the government and their allies. The State Department has also enacted visa restrictions targeting more than 2,350 Nicaraguan officials and their family members.

Volker Türk, the United Nations' high commissioner for human rights, denounced Nicaragua's legislative ambitions on Wednesday, saying that "people of all political viewpoints must be allowed to vote and run for office."
"These latest developments further deepen the severe restrictions on fundamental freedoms, the dismantling of civic space, and the steady erosion of the rule of law," Türk said in a statement.
The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Israeli UN envoy blasts Mamdani as 'clown' over call to arrest Netanyahu: 'It's a stunt'
summary: Israel's UN ambassador called Mayor Zohran Mamdani a "clown" after he demanded federal authorities arrest Benjamin Netanyahu on an ICC warrant.
story: Thiessen criticizes Mamdani for calling on federal authorities to arrest Netanyahu on an International Criminal Court warrant despite a lack of legal authority.

Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations on Wednesday blasted New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani as a "clown" for demanding federal authorities arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu when Netanyahu arrives in the city.

Danny Danon’s remarks came after Mamdani accused Netanyahu of being a "war criminal" and the "architect of a horrific genocide" against Palestinians while calling on the federal government to execute an International Criminal Court arrest warrant against the Israeli leader.
Netanyahu is scheduled to address the United Nations General Assembly in Manhattan in September.
NETANYAHU FIRES BACK AT NYC MAYOR MAMDANI'S VOW TO ENFORCE 'BOGUS ARREST WARRANT'

Israeli Ambassador to the U.N. Danny Danon speaks during a United Nations emergency security council meeting on Lebanon at the U.N. Headquarters in New York, on Mar. 31. (Charly Triballeau/AFP via Getty Images)
"Those baseless remarks about harassing the prime minister — it's a joke, and he's a clown," Danon told Fox News Digital Wednesday.

"Everyone knows it's a show. It's a stunt," Danon added. "A mayor should be dealing with the homeless people, the garbage in New York, and leave foreign affairs to the people in Washington who are elected to do it. He should take care of the security of the people in New York, especially the Jewish community, which is seeing the rise of antisemitism. That is his first responsibility."
The YouTube channel for the New York City Mayor's Office released a video July 21, "Benjamin Netanyahu is a war criminal."
"Benjamin Netanyahu is a war criminal, the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people," Mamdani said, repeating comments he made in an interview with The New York Times.

Mamdani leveled a series of allegations against the Israeli leader, claiming he was "responsible for the killing of more than 73,000 people, for the maiming of tens of thousands of children, as those who survive undergo amputation without anesthesia."
He also accused Netanyahu of targeting neonatal hospitals and maternity care centers and alleged that he blocked food and humanitarian aid.
CNN LEGAL ANALYST CALLS OUT 'UTTERLY RIDICULOUS' CLAIM BY MAMDANI ABOUT NETANYAHU ARREST
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks to reporters during a news conference in New York on Feb. 17, 2026.  (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)

"Just last month, the U.N. confirmed that Palestinian children continue to be deliberately targeted and killed by Israeli armed forces, more than eight months after the so-called ceasefire," Mamdani said.
"All as we, as Americans, pay for the bombs that do the killing. There is a reason the International Criminal Court issued a warrant for his arrest."
Danon pushed back sharply against the mayor's accusations.
"There is a lot of humanitarian aid coming into Gaza every day," Danon argued.

"Nobody speaks about those issues anymore, but he wants to resume spreading blood libels, promoting the claims of genocide, starvation and all those lies that were spread by him, by his wife and by other people during the war.
"He wants to go back to this situation, but today there are no humanitarian issues in Gaza," Danon added.
"Mamdani continues to promote those blood libels against Israel and against the Jews."
Mamdani also said that City Hall cannot act on the warrant unilaterally.

"It is clear that we do not have the independent legal authority to enforce this warrant. The federal government, however, does, and I call on them to join the ICC and execute this warrant," Mamdani said.
"Benjamin Netanyahu is not welcome in New York City, nor is any other war criminal at large."
MAMDANI’S ‘DERANGED’ ISRAEL TAKE RESURFACES AS HE TARGETS NETANYAHU

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said his administration is exploring whether the city has legal authority to arrest Netanyahu, pictured here, if he visits for the U.N. General Assembly. (Ronen Zvulun/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)
Israeli officials strongly deny all charges. Netanyahu’s office has rejected the ICC’s jurisdiction, labeling it "a kangaroo court that has no jurisdiction over Americans or Israelis."

"People are smart; they know there's no legal basis for his remarks," Danon said. "The U.S. is not part of the ICC. There is no warrant that is actually effective against the prime minister in the U.S. So it's a political stunt."
"We have serious issues to deal with — the war with Iran and other critical matters.
"The prime minister is not actually dealing with Mamdani's remarks at all. He said it very clearly: He intends to come and speak at the U.N.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Prime Minister Netanyahu will come to New York and will speak in the General Assembly," Danon said. "The only thing the mayor can do is come to the U.N., grab a seat, listen to the Prime Minister and maybe learn something from his speech.
