Any of the details that they want to share, they can share,” Kelce, who’s also a field hockey coach, said on the podcast. “Otherwise, it was intimate, and incredible, and full of love both for each other and for everybody’s else love for them.”

Kylie Kelce, who’s been married to former NFL player Jason Kelce since 2018, shares four children with the former athlete. She’s been mum about the wedding as the couple themselves have not publicly revealed much either.

During her podcast episode, Kelce called out Us Weekly, saying that the outlet had published a snippet of a private conversation that she had had with a father and daughter at recent event. During that conversation, the fans had asked if photos of the wedding would be shared, Kelce said.
“And I said, ‘Well it just happened, you gotta give them some time to bask in it. They’re in the honeymoon time,’” Kelce recalled on her podcast.
However, Kelce said, the outlet recorded and posted a piece of the conversation, claiming that she was “seen discussing Taylor Swift’s wedding.”
Us Weekly did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment.
“Don’t eavesdrop on my conversations,” she said during the episode, encouraging people to head to her podcast for her actual thoughts.
“If you want to hear something from me, you can come right here,” Kelce said, referencing her podcast. “Straight from the horse’s mouth.”
Donna Kelce, the mother of the groom, appears to have had the same exact takeaway from the royal wedding.
During the Macy’s fireworks show on July 4, the day after the big event, the proud mom said that she couldn’t “say a heck of a lot, except it was magical, man.”
It certainly sounded like that day was a fairytale.

title: ‘Odyssey’ Fans Are Facing Weeks Of Sold-Out Shows. Here’s How To Get Tickets
summary: For fans looking to snag a highly-coveted seat to an IMAX showing of “The Odyssey,” the search for tickets has been challenging. But it’s not impossible, experts say.
story: For fans looking to snag a highly-coveted seat to an IMAX showing of “The Odyssey,” the struggle has been way too real. But experts have some tips and tricks to increase moviegoers’ chances to catch the famously sold-out film.

The nearly three-hour film, directed by Christopher Nolan, was released on July 17. Since, many of the showings have been completely booked or only have a few openings left, as fans clamber to see the first movie shot entirely on IMAX 70 millimeter.

In many cases, getting a spot to one of the showings of the movie on 70mm IMAX involves an extremely long wait.  In New York City and Los Angeles, where there few theaters that offer the film in that format, no tickets are available through mid-August, according to Variety. The wait is even longer in London, where screenings are sold out through Sept. 10, the outlet reported.

TODAY.com spoke to several movie and ticket industry experts on why the film has drawn such extreme crowds and if there’s any — literally any — possible way to nab a good seat at an IMAX showing these days.

“This is one of the oldest stories ever told, and it’s being told by a man who is arguably our most important and our biggest director filmmaker working today,” Erik Davis, movie commentator at Fandango, tells TODAY.com. “There’s not many movies during the year where it almost feels like everyone is collectively going to see it, but this is definitely one of those movies.”
As movie fans look to catch a showing of Homer’s work brought to life, here’s what industry experts say about the film and finding those somewhat-elusive tickets.
Why Are Tickets to “The Odyssey” So Hard to Get?

Already, “The Odyssey” has proven itself to be the blockbuster of the summer. According to Universal Pictures, the production company behind the major movie, the project grossed $264.1 million globally in ticket sales its opening weekend.

Experts say that it’s not necessarily a surprise that the film has drawn so much buzz. For starters, the cast — which includes the likes of Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Tom Holland and so many more — is stacked, Davis points out. And each star comes with their own fans. Additionally, Davis says that the story itself is not only a highly-acclaimed masterpiece that’s thousands of years old, but it’s also being brought to life in a way that feels revolutionary.

“There’s a feeling that it’s like the modern day version of a film like ‘Lawrence of Arabia,’” Davis says, referencing the critically acclaimed 1962 film, which was largely heralded as one of the best historical epics for its cutting-edge cinematography and rich storytelling. “Everything’s shot on location, everything is real and all of the effects are practical effects.
Davis explains that the confluence of factors “screams, ‘This is the reason why we go to the movies! This is what we’re looking for.’”

There’s also the issue of IMAX venues, says Michael Amouyal, senior director of marketing and partnerships at movie ticketing app Atom Tickets. Because the film is the first to be shot entirely on 70mm IMAX, people want to see it in its intended format, Amouyal explains. But theaters that feature the movie in that format are few and far between — 25 venues across the U.S. to be exact. And people want to witness history, with some driving hours or hitting up the questionable resale market for a chance to see the epic, Amouyal says.

“It’s very clear in the marketing you’ve seen — the national marketing, the TV ads, the posters that are up — that that is very front and center,” Amouyal says of 70mm IMAX. “They’ve gotten people really, really excited about the format … that format specifically is not as available across the country.”
So How the Heck Do You Get Tickets? Try This Trick

However, the experts underscored, it’s not impossible to get tickets — or even good seats. It’s all about where you look. For starters, Amouyal says that many of the extra crowded or sold-out showings are the ones that are done in premium, large formats (PFL), where everything is bigger, louder and bolder. Though tickets to primetime showings on weekends in other formats are also in high demand, there is a higher chance that people can snag some seats.

“Some people don’t have any of those premium format theaters within an hour of their home, so they can still go and find tickets for the film at laser or other standard projection formats,” Amouyal says. “It still captures the scale and the vision of the film.”
He adds, laughing, that “your ears may not be ringing afterwards, but some people don’t necessarily need that.”

For those determined to experience the film on IMAX, not all hope is lost. If you weren’t lucky enough to snatch a ticket during the very limited presale last year or the more recent June 4 presale for PLF showings, some experts recommend checking for seats closer to showtime. Keith Pagello, founder of ticketing data and price history site TicketData, says that when it comes to purchasing tickets from movie theater sites, “refresh, refresh, refresh, refresh again.”
The sweet spot, Pagello says, is generally around 24 hours before showtime and again around one to two hours prior to the desired showing. Aspiring moviegoers might just get lucky.

“AMC allows refunds based on any ticket. So I think what you’re seeing is that a lot of people, when the second tickets went on sale, just bought maybe four tickets even though they only had two people that were intending to go,” Pagello says. “Then the show’s approaching and they actually only need two tickets.”

For every show, he adds, there’s generally a handful of tickets that are released at one point or another because of canceled purchases. In other cases, theaters may have inventory that they had held back and reserved for different individuals, who may no longer be able to attend, he says. As tedious as it is, “just keep refreshing,” Pagello says.

Davis explains that fans will also have better luck with IMAX showings outside of primetime viewing hours. Late night screenings, for example, in addition to early or weeknight screenings have a chance as well, he says. But it’s important to remember that the film is still in its first few weekends of showings and that seats will open up as time goes on.

However, if you’re itching to see the film now, Davis encourages viewers to stay open-minded when it comes to seating. If a spot toward the front of the theater opens up for a 70mm IMAX showing, for example, take it!

“What’s interesting with IMAX 70 millimeter screens is that because the screen is so large, the seats really are set back,” Davis says. “I myself sat in row C for IMAX 70 screening of ‘The Odyssey’ in New York. It was great, and I had no problem and it didn’t feel like I was too close to the screen.”
Beware of Scammers

Because of the competition for tickets, particularly for 70mm IMAX showings, people have resorted to unorthodox ways to see the film, sometimes falling prey to scalpers and scammers. A moderator for subreddit r/NYCmovies told Variety that they’ve noticed alarming behavior from those looking to get the best of some enthusiastic cinephiles.

“The worst thing are users pretending to have tickets they don’t have at all. Again, once reported, we ban, but they often just make new accounts,” the moderator told the outlet. “We are warning people to be careful and check post history, get proof of tickets, if possible do an in-person exchange (if you print the ticket on a kiosk you know you have a legit ticket that can no longer be double sold or refunded), and if you do an online transaction, turn on PayPal’s Goods & Services protection feature.”
Pagello warns fans to stay away from any Craigslist listings, claiming to offer tickets, or social media posts.

“I would definitely suggest a lot of hesitancy if somebody’s thinking about doing that, or flat out just say that it’s probably not something that you should be doing,” Pagello says. “You’re probably better off to keep refreshing and try to buy directly from the theater.”
Just Because You Can’t Get in Now, Doesn’t Mean You’ll Never Be Able to See the Film in Theaters

There’s one particular upside to the film’s popularity, experts explain. With the outpouring of demand, many theaters will add extra screenings, Davis says. And theaters are more likely to extend the film’s run a few additional weeks as well.

While the film is quite the experience in theaters, Davis adds, those who miss the window to watch it at the movies can always wait to see it when it comes out on streaming. It’s still worth it, he says.

“First and foremost, even if you have to wait a couple of weeks until the demand dries out a little bit, I would go to see it in theaters,” he says. “That being said, it’s a fantastic film. If you wind up watching this at home, I still think you’re going to get a lot out of the movie, the film speaks for itself. The performances speak for themselves.”

title: 10 Years Ago, She Was Framed for an Unspeakable Crime. How Michelle Hadley Is Now
summary: Who is Michelle Hadley? Where is she now? Here’s what she said about the Toxic Love Story case.
story: A series of menacing emails, stunning accusations and a jaw-dropping twist are all part of a years-long legal saga involving a California woman who spent months in jail before police learned she had been framed.
The saga surrounding Michelle Hadley is the subject of the new Netflix true crime documentary “A Toxic Love Story,” which begins streaming on July 23. Hadley appears in the film to share her ordeal.

The Anaheim resident went from spending nearly three months in jail to being vindicated after investigators found she was framed in a scheme perpetrated in 2016 after she ended a two-year relationship with a U.S. marshal.
In a 2017 interview on TODAY, she called the situation “horrifying.”
“It is really like your worst nightmare coming true,” she said.
Here’s what to know about the case and how Hadley is doing now.
A Breakup Followed by Threatening Emails
A 2017 news release by the Orange County District Attorney’s Office details Hadley’s ordeal and its shocking turn.
In 2013, Hadley began dating Ian Diaz, a U.S. marshal she had met on a dating website.
The two purchased a condominium together after a whirlwind romance, but the relationship soured in August 2015, resulting in Hadley moving out.
Diaz then got married to his wife, Angela Diaz, in February 2016 after meeting her on the same dating website. In May 2016, Angela said she was pregnant with twins, per the news release.

On June 1, 2016, Ian and Angela Diaz made a stunning accusation to the Anaheim Police Department: someone with the online handle “LilithisTruth” had been sending Angela emails threatening to have her raped and attaching graphic images of dead and decapitated bodies and aborted fetuses. The couple said the anonymous emailer was Hadley.
Angela Diaz also claimed that Hadley was impersonating her online and soliciting men on Craigslist to come to Diaz’s home to engage in a “rape fantasy” with her.
Angela Diaz called 911 on June 24, 2016, and reported that a man tried to rape her in the garage of the condo. She greeted police with a ripped shirt and redness on her neck and breast area.
Hadley said on TODAY in 2017 that she had never met Diaz before the accusations and “had no idea who she was, and out of the blue, I’m getting a restraining order from her.”
What Happened to Michelle Hadley?

Hadley, who was a 29-year-old graduate student at the time, was arrested by police on June 24, 2016, and was bailed out the following day, according to the 2017 news release by the Orange County District Attorney’s Office.

Angela Diaz claimed that the emails and rape solicitation fantasies stopped when Hadley was in custody, but resumed after she made bail. On July 13, Anaheim police intercepted a 17-year-old boy outside Diaz’s home who admitted to thinking the Craigslist ad for a “rape fantasy” was real.

A day later, an arrest warrant for Hadley was issued, charging her with felony stalking with a restraining order, stalking, criminal threats, attempted rape, assault with the intent to commit rape during a residential burglary, violating a protective order, and a crime-bail-crime enhancement. The charges carried a potential life sentence in prison, and she was held in jail on $1 million bail while proclaiming her innocence.
“I got the sense that (police) did not want to hear my side of the story,” Hadley said on TODAY in 2017.

At the time, police based their charges against Hadley on the fact that religious tones used in the emails were similar to emails Hadley had sent Ian Diaz after their breakup in 2015, plus the fact that real men were showing up to Diaz’s condo due to the Craigslist ad. In addition, the emails contained Hadley’s verified email address and other personal facts, and the police also had the report from Angela Diaz’s 911 call claiming she was attacked.
“We believe our actions were appropriate based on the evidence that was known to us at the time,” the Anaheim Police Department said in a statement to TODAY in 2017.
Hadley communicated to third parties at the time that she believed she was being set up.
A Stunning Twist and Shocking Arrest
An investigation by the Anaheim Police Department led to an eye-opening revelation: Angela Diaz had been the one sending the emails to herself in order to frame Hadley.

In January 2017, Angela Diaz was charged with two counts of kidnapping, two counts of false imprisonment, perjury, two counts of forgery, two counts of possession of forged instrument, grand theft, one misdemeanor count of filing a false report with an agency and 21 misdemeanor counts of filing a false police report, according to a news release by the Orange County District Attorney’s Office.
Hadley was exonerated of all her charges after spending 88 days in jail. She was released on Oct. 7, 2016.

“It is often said that true life is stranger than fiction. The facts of this case make that statement spot on,” the district attorney’s office said in the news release. “When a person who has committed a crime gets arrested and charged, that’s a bad day! But when someone who is innocent gets arrested and charged with some crime, that’s not just a bad day — it’s a nightmare!”

Diaz was accused of pretending to be Hadley and sending the threatening emails and rape fantasy solicitations to herself. The investigation found that the emails originated from the condominium Diaz shared with her husband, plus her cell phone and her father’s home in Arizona.

The investigation also uncovered unrelated fraudulent activity by Diaz, including faking cervical cancer, pretending to be an attorney, forging doctor’s notes, faking a pregnancy and impersonating another one of her husband’s ex-girlfriends over email, according to the news release.

Angela Diaz was sentenced to five years in state prison in California in October 2017 after pleading guilty to felony kidnapping, false imprisonment by menace, fraud or deceit, forgery, perjury, grand theft and misdemeanors for falsely reporting a crime, according to a news release by the Orange County District Attorney’s Office.

“It is unfathomable why Ms. Diaz would concoct such a diabolical scheme to hurt an innocent person,” District Attorney Tony Rackauckas said in a statement in the 2017 news release. “Even while pleading guilty, Diaz showed no remorse, compassion, or empathy for the victim.”
Five Years Later, Another Arrest in the Case
The guilty plea from Angela Diaz was not the end of the story.

At the time that local police departments were investigating Angela Diaz in 2017, the Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General (DOJ-OIG) Cyber Investigations Office opened an investigation against Ian Diaz, who was a U.S. marshal.

Federal investigators found that Ian Diaz collaborated with his wife on the email hoax and the calls to law enforcement to frame Hadley, according to a 2023 news release by the DOJ-OIG. The investigation also found that Ian Diaz took steps to conceal their actions, including using falsely registered email accounts, virtual private networks and encrypted messaging services.

More than five years after the attempt to frame Hadley, Ian Diaz was arrested in 2021 on multiple charges. In March 2023, he was convicted by a jury of one count of conspiracy to commit cyberstalking, one count of cyberstalking, one count of perjury and one count of obstructing a federal proceeding.

In June 2023, Ian Diaz was sentenced to 10 years in federal prison and three years of supervised release for his role in the hoax, according to a news release by the U.S. Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General.
The mystery of why Ian Diaz took part in the frame attempt on Hadley is examined in the Neftlix documentary but remains unclear.
During his federal trial, prosecutors said he did it as part of a twisted plot to force Hadley to walk away from the condo they bought together, according to NBC News.
“To me, it’s about the condo, because otherwise, what threat am I? I was out of the picture,” Hadley said on TODAY in 2017.
Neither Ian nor Angela Diaz participated in the Netflix documentary.
Where Is Michelle Hadley Now?
Hadley filed a civil lawsuit against the Anaheim Police Department and four of its officers in 2018, alleging that they rushed to charge her.

“The Anaheim Police Department and its officers abdicated their duties to adhere to investigative norms, instead conspiring to do the bidding of a corrupt federal marshal,” the lawsuit said, according to NBC News. “They appear to have willingly become Ian Diaz’s weapon in his tortious campaign to ruin the life of his ex-girlfriend, plaintiff Michelle Hadley.”
Hadley made similar claims in her 2017 interview on TODAY.
“I believe that the police had enough information available to them before they arrested me the first time to know it wasn’t me doing it,” she said.
Hadley accepted a settlement from the city of Anaheim for an undisclosed amount in April 2021, according to Courthouse News.
Attorneys for the city of Anaheim said in court documents that the officers had probable cause to believe Hadley was behind the attacks at first, per Courthouse News.
After the winding legal saga culminated with Ian Diaz’s conviction by a federal jury in 2023, Hadley shared a statement with NBC News.

“I am so grateful to the (Justice Department Office of Inspector General) for the work they put into this case and to the jury for a conviction that has brought so much peace to my family and restored some of the faith we lost in the justice system as a result of Diaz’s crimes against me,” she said.
On the same day Ian Diaz was convicted in 2023, Hadley gave birth to a baby girl.

“My life has been filled by strange, often symbolic, and sometimes beautiful coincidences like this,” Hadley told NBC News. “My daughter represents my rainbow after a very long storm, and my heart has never felt so full.”

title: I’m a Black Greek Woman. What Lupita Nyong’o’s Casting as Helen of Troy in ‘The Odyssey’ Meant to Me
summary: Evelin Boatenk, who is of Black and Ghanaian descent, reacts to Lupita Nyong’o’s casting as Helen of Troy in The Odyssey.
story: Evelin Boatenk walked into a screening of “The Odyssey” on a Thursday night — and left the theater completely changed.
“It was 100% a healing experience,” Boatenk, an influencer and owner of a social media brand, tells TODAY.com of Christopher Nolan’s interpretation of the ancient Homeric poem.

The daughter of a Greek-Polish mother and a Ghanaian father, Boatenk was raised in Thessaloniki, Greece’s second-largest city, by her mom and her maternal grandparents. She grew up speaking Greek, cooking Greek food and listening to her grandfather read mythology as a bedtime story.
Still, because of her skin color, she felt she was not Greek “enough.” As the only Black girl in her public school, Boatenk says she always felt different.
“No one ever asked me out in school. I never went on a date. I never felt like I wasn’t beautiful, but I did not understand how beautiful I was until I started traveling,” she says.
A trip to Paris changed everything. “It was the first time I saw many Black people. I was like, ‘What’s going on here? What is this place? I love it,’” she says.

Eventually, Boatenk left Greece to chase more of that feeling. It was a bittersweet decision; though she loves Greece, she says, the country doesn’t represent “100%” of who she is — “and many of them are not even OK with what I am.”
She moved to New York in 2024 and has since married.

“I always wanted to be somewhere that I’m not the ‘only one.’ I can do my thing without always having someone pointing at me like, ‘Ah, Evelin — the Black girl?’ Here, I am Evelin, and I’m smart, and I’m all the things without anyone saying ‘the Black girl,’” she says.

Recently, Boatenk began sharing her experiences about being Black and Greek on social media. While she felt she encountered racism growing up in Greece in the ’90s, she says what she experiences online now is more intense. “I had racist comments, but they were not as harsh and as direct as what I see now,” she says, with people often saying she is “not Greek.”

Despite facing what she calls “ignorance” from commenters, she says she’s “so happy” she shared her experiences. “I found so many people who are like me. People who are Greek and Dominican, Greek and Cuban. I found a guy who is Greek and Ghanaian!” she says.

Given her upbringing, when Lupita Nyong’o, an actor who was born in Kenya and raised in Mexico, was cast as Helen of Troy in Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” Boatenk braced herself for backlash — and it came. The movie also sparked criticism in Greece because Nolan didn’t cast actors of Greek ethnic descent.
But “The Odyssey” came out on July 17 to rave reviews and box office wins.

Boatenk was astonished by Nyong’o and the rest of the cast, which she called inclusive. On the casting discussion front, some people have argued that, since “The Odyssey” is a myth, Nolan can have creative agency.
But for Boatenk, the movie’s diversity doesn’t strike her as fantastical; it is her lived experience.

“There are people that are Black and Greek, Asian and Greek. Mixed race people exist. It’s time for the world to actually accept them and accept that not every European country is plainly white,” she says.

This is especially true of Helen of Troy. “I didn’t feel like she does not belong to the film. For me, it was very natural to see a Black woman playing a Greek woman, because this is exactly who I am.”
She knows that if a younger Evelin could have seen “The Odyssey,” she would have asked, “Mom, was Helen Black like me?”
“I would see myself. I would feel (like), ‘Little Evelin, you are not the only one. There are people like you,’” she says.
As someone who grew up studying Homer in school and feeling like the odd woman out, she says this movie “closed the circle.”
“Now I see a movie that is a Greek story with so many different people with different backgrounds. It makes me so very proud and happy. I felt seen,” she says.

title: Please Don’t Do This 1 Thing After Reading ‘The Correspondent,’ Author Virginia Evans Requests
summary: Author Virginia Evans asks readers not to do this after reading “The Correspondent” — don’t write to Ann Patchett.
story: “The Correspondent” is a novel about a woman who writes letters. But its author, Virginia Evans, has a plea for readers inspired to do the same: Don’t write to Ann Patchett.

Patchett, also a bestselling novelist, has a “bone to pick” with Evans over the number of letters she’s received from “The Correspondent” readers, Evans told Jenna Bush Hager on the July 23 episode of her “Open Book With Jenna” podcast.

In the novel, Sybil regularly writes to her literary heroes. Patchett is among the few who write back, and the two form a pen pal relationship in the book. But readers shouldn’t follow Sybil’s exact lead, the author warned.
“Ann has a bone to pick with me because I included her in the book, people are writing to her,” Evans told Jenna. “So if you’re listening to this, write (to) someone else. Don’t write to Ann.”
The author went on to double down on her plea: “She won’t write back,” she said. “I promise you, anytime I’m interviewed from now on, I’ll be like, ‘Don’t write to Ann.’”

But, in the same breath, Evans acknowledged that around 10 years ago she wrote to Patchett herself to share thoughts on one of her novels. Since then, the two have maintained a close relationship — the longest Patchett has kept with a person who has “written to her out of the blue,” Evans said.

“I think we just are kindred spirits or something … She just loved me from afar and cared about me and cared about my life and invested a little bit of time in me,” Evans explained, adding that she experienced many life challenges throughout her 30s during their years as pen pals.
Evans had written multiple novels before “The Correspondent” was published and eventually became a major hit.
“That decade, she was kind to me, and let me tell her about the sorrow and tell her about the joy,” Evans told Jenna, in part. “She just had my back.”
While Jenna echoed Evans’ plea that readers do not write to Patchett, she also shared that she and the “Whistler” author are pen pals too — or more accurately, email pals.
Jenna added that she should print those emails somewhere so she doesn’t lose them, perhaps a reasonable precaution, given how sought-after a letter has become from the author.

title: Jennifer Garner Describes ‘Interesting Relationship’ With the 2 Paparazzi Assigned to Her for 20 Years
summary: Jennifer Garner, an A-lister parent, revealed a time where, feeling unsafe, she once turned to a surprising but familiar face: her longtime paparazzo.
story: Jennifer Garner, an A-lister parent, revealed a time where, feeling unsafe, she once turned to a surprising but familiar face: her longtime paparazzo.

Garner is an advocate for public safety laws in the state of California when it comes to paparazzi around children. In 2013, she joined fellow actor Halle Berry to testify at a California State Assembly Committee on Public Safety hearing to support a bill that would penalize taking photos of children without permission.

That bill was signed into law in September 2013. Asked to reflect on the “current landscape” of paparazzi culture years later, Garner described her personal experience with the camerapeople who’ve followed her for over two decades.

“I have two every day who’ve been assigned to me for 20-plus years, 25 years,” Garner said on the July 21 episode of Evan Ross Katz’s podcast, “Shut Up Evan.” “It’s really interesting. I have a very interesting relationship with my main guy. ... We have an odd respect for each other. We’ve had some really real-life moments together.”
Garner described a specific instance where, despite having “done anything to ask him to leave” over the years, she felt unsafe and turned to him for help.
“I was followed by someone who, for whatever reason, I thought was going to hurt me, and I ran to him because I knew him and trusted him, and I knew that he and I would be OK,” Garner said.

“There’s kind of a Stockholm Syndrome kind of thing,” she added. “And at the same time, I’ve called the cops on him a million times, and been like, ‘Can you please just give me a walk around the block with my kids and my dog?’”
Earlier on the podcast, Garner discussed the invasive environment that developed around her life and the particular danger facing her children.

“Kids were at the center of it. I lived on the street with a lot of much more famous and successful people than I, but they followed me because I had the kids,” Garner said. “They wouldn’t follow Ben (Affleck). They wouldn’t follow Matt Damon.”

Garner and Affleck, who divorced in 2018, share and co-parent three children together: Violet, 20, Fin, 17, and Samuel, 14. Garner opened up about the dangerous situations that paparazzi presence created at their children’s schools.
“Kids were getting knocked over coming out of preschool by photographers who were so hungry to get to me or to Ben, trying to get to our kids,” Garner said. “You don’t belong at a school, you know?”
Garner even said one of her children was asked to leave a soccer league because of all the cars that would surround the area.
“It was a danger to everyone around us,” she said. “If I went through a yellow light, 15 cars would go through the red behind me.”

title: ‘Die Hard’ Turns 38. Watch Bruce Willis Discuss His Iconic Role in 1988 TODAY Interview
summary: In the latest TODAY Vault, Bruce Willis on TODAY in 1988, just days before the release of the first “Die Hard.”
story: Welcome inside the TODAY Vault, where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Bruce Willis on TODAY with Bryant Gumbel on July 13 and 14, 1988, just days before the release of the first “Die Hard.”
Bruce Willis’ professional life changed forever July 22, 1988, when “Die Hard” hit theaters. A month later, his personal life followed suit when he became a father for the first time.
Heading into that summer, Willis was best known as the star of TV’s “Moonlighting,” who had previously dipped his toe into film with flops like “Blind Date” and “Sunset.” Then came “Die Hard.”

The action genre shifted after the release of “Die Hard,” with the film destined to become a classic. It was also the first in a franchise that spanned decades — not to mention the age-old argument about whether the original is indeed a Christmas movie.

Willis promoted the “Die Hard” during a two-day appearance on TODAY on July 13 and 14, 1988, in which Bryant Gumbel seemed to dance around the edges of how the film would find its place in a world dominated by other action stars, not knowing that it would eventually become the standard by which other action movies that followed would be judged.
What Did Bruce Willis Say About ‘Die Hard’?
Willis hadn’t yet reached the rarified air of an action star at the time, but Gumbel asked a question that, in hindsight, hinted at how his star would rise.
“Does it bother you that this film is going to be compared to all of (Sylvester) Stallone’s and all of (Arnold) Schwarzenegger’s and all of (Chuck) Norris’ efforts?” Gumbel asked.

“Not really. I think it’s inevitable. It’s an action film,” Willis said. “I think what makes our film different is that it’s an adventure, too. And also it’s about people, I think, the audience can relate to. These aren’t larger-than-life characters. These are, for the most part, ordinary people.”
Willis Had Quite the Response When Asked About His Salary
20th Century-Fox reportedly paid Willis $5 million for the movie, a stunning sum at the time especially since he was not yet a bankable star.
“This throws the business out of whack,” late then-MGM Chairman Alan Ladd Jr. said about the salary, a comment Gumbel brought up to Willis.
“I’d like to ask Alan Ladd how much money he made last year. I don’t think he’d tell you,” he said.

“I don’t think it’s anybody’s business how much money I make. And if I upset Alan Ladd Jr.’s apple cart, then that’s showbiz, Alan. What can I do, Bryant?” he said. “...Fox paid me what they thought I was worth to them.”

The paychecks — and the films — would only get bigger for Willis, who would go on to star in the four “Die Hard” flicks that followed. Then there were hits like “Armageddon,” “The Sixth Sense,” “Looper,” “Pulp Fiction,” “Sin City” and “The Fifth Element.”
Willis Was on the Verge of Landing a New Role: Dad

Becoming one of the biggest movie stars in the world was only the beginning for Willis in the summer of 1988. He and then-wife Demi Moore would welcome Rumer, the first of their three daughters, when she was born Aug. 16. Willis and current wife Emma Heming Willis also share two daughters.
Before he officially became a girl dad for the first time, Willis told Gumbel he was “anxious” about Rumer’s arrival and admitted he couldn’t grasp how much his world was going to change.
“I keep thinking that nothing can prepare you for that, you know, that it’s just, no matter how wild you think it is, that it’s gonna be 10 times that,” he said.
Willis, who has kept a lower profile since being diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia in 2023 following a 2022 aphasia diagnosis, also had a good sense that he was entering uncharted territory.
“I really think that no matter how well I can get ready for it, we’re going to make mistakes. Parents make mistakes, I think. I don’t think anybody can really do it perfectly,” he said.

title: Prince George Turns 13! See Proud Parents Prince William and Kate Middleton Celebrate the Teenager
summary: Prince George is now a teenager and turned 13 on July 22. Read his parents sweet post celebrating the milestone birthday.
story: Prince George is now a teenager!
Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, celebrated Prince George’s milestone 13th birthday with a sweet message on their official Instagram account Wednesday, July 22.

“Happy 13th Birthday, George! 🎉” they captioned a photo of their oldest child, decked out in a dark blazer, pants and white button-down shirt. In the new portrait, he sports a slight smile with his hands in his pockets.

The couple also shared a video of George on a beach playing with his younger brother, petting his dog and swinging a cricket bat, with the caption, “Thank you for all the birthday wishes for George today!”
The royal couple are also parents to Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, 8.

The former Kate Middleton and her husband reveal special family photos of their children every year to mark their birthdays. Last year for the now-teen’s special day, the Prince and Princess of Wales’ official Instagram account shared a video of the three siblings holding hands. Prince George and Princess Charlotte also carried their younger brother and laughed in the clip.

The family recently attended the Men’s 2026 Wimbledon Final on July 12. Prince William, Kate, George and Charlotte sat in the Royal Box as they watched World No. 1 Jannik Sinner defend his title and secure the championship trophy for the second year in a row. Prince Louis did not attend the event.

After his win, Sinner was seen chatting with the family. In a video shared on ESPN’s YouTube page, the star athlete asked the children if they practice tennis every day. George and Charlotte shared that they usually practice on the weekends.

Shortly after the final, the Prince and Princess of Wales shared a congratulatory post on Instagram, featuring a video of the family cheering at the event. George appeared almost as tall as mom Kate in the footage.
“A brilliant Men’s Final at The Championships. Congratulations @janniksin on a superb performance and a well-earned @wimbledon title!” the caption read.

Prince George’s 13th birthday comes after a Kensington Palace spokesperson confirmed to NBC News in June that he is set to follow in his father’s footsteps and attend Eton College starting in September.

Eton College is a private boarding school in Windsor, England, that was founded in 1440 by King Henry VI. In addition to Prince William, former British Prime Ministers Robert Walpole, David Cameron and Boris Johnson studied there, as well as uncle Prince Harry and great-uncle Earl Charles Spencer.

title: I’m a ‘Love Island USA’ Fanatic. Here’s What to Watch Next to Fill the Void
summary: What shows are like Love Island USA? Here are the shows and specific seasons to watch now that Love Island USA season 8 is over.
story: Take it From Me is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this latest installment, “Love Island USA” superfans share their top reality shows that will have viewers hooked all summer long.
“Love Island USA” has officially come to an end, which means fans now have six-days worth of free time they need to fill.

Season 8 of the hit Peacock series wrapped July 12, with Bryce Alakai and Trinity Tatum being named the winners. But with that happy, romantic ending came the sad realization that it will be months until fans hear “I got a text,” watch contestants compete in a series of make out-filled challenges and witness intense recouplings.

Superfans Mike Gauyo (@blackboywrites), Adrianna (@adriannasmiles) and Kristi Cook (@spillsesh), who spent the last six weeks posting about the show on social media, racking up millions of views and likes, are also feeling the absence of “Love Island USA.”
So, they’ve shared with TODAY.com their recommendations on the next binge-worthy shows to keep reality television lovers busy the rest of the summer.
Read on for a list of specific shows and seasons that these superfans consider “must-see” television.
‘The Traitors’ Seasons 3 and 4
If you are looking for a show that has even more drama and a strategic element, then you might want to check out Peacock’s “The Traitors.”

The series brings together current reality television stars and legends, and places them in a Scottish castle. There, they compete as Faithfuls and Traitors. The Faithfuls must determine who among them are the Traitors, a group that secretly meets every night to plot their next murder. Every episode, a contestant is banished and must reveal their true identity. The series is packed with fun challenges and impressive game play, all culminating in a grand finale where one or multiple players win the cash prize.
Television writer and content creator Gauyo tells TODAY.com that “The Traitors” Season 4, which was released earlier this year, was his “all-time favorite” season of a reality television show.
“That season was must-see TV, especially the finale with Rob Rausch and Maura Higgins tête-à-tête for the prize money,” he says, referring to two stars of the “Love Island” franchise.

Content creator Adrianna agrees that “The Traitors” is one of the best reality television shows, highlighting Seasons 3 and 4 specifically. She described the series as her “favorite game of deception” thanks to a cast filled with “reality stars from all types of shows, from ‘Survivor’ to ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race’ to ‘Love Island.’”
“Think of ‘Clue’ meets ‘Knives Out’ meets ‘Show Me the Money,’” she continues. “It’s entertaining week after week because you never know who will be eliminated next.”
Those who already watched “The Traitors” have the civilian-only version to look forward to. Gauyo says he’ll be tuning in when “The Traitors: New Blood” premieres this fall on NBC on Sept. 17.
‘Big Brother’ Season 28
If you enjoy “Love Island USA” mostly because you get to see what the islanders are up to nearly every day (except hump day), then “Big Brother” might be the show for you.

The CBS staple kicked off its 28th season on July 9, introducing 14 new houseguests and three reality television icons. “Big Brother” airs three nights a week but fans can also watch all the alliances and backdoor plans form in real-time thanks to the show’s 24/7 live feeds. With the feeds, fans experience key moments, providing context that is sometimes missing from the show.
Gauyo recommends catching up on the current season since only a few episodes have aired.

Content creator Kristi Cook of Spill Sesh is a fan of the series, too. She notes the multiple episodes per week and the “addictive social dynamics and nonstop twists” of “Big Brother” will draw “Love Island USA” viewers in.
“The live feeds mean there’s almost always something to watch even when new episodes aren’t on,” she adds.
‘Love Island UK’ Seasons 12 and 13
If you are interested in checking out other versions of “Love Island,” you should start with the flagship UK series.
“For those who haven’t watched the UK version of Love Island, I highly recommend watching the last season that just aired. So good,” Gauyo praises.

Season 12, or “series” as they say across the pond, welcomed the first-ever American contestant to the UK version, which takes place at a villa in Mallorca, Spain. Toni Laites, the first bombshell of the season, was a server from Las Vegas who wasn’t afraid to ruffle feathers from the moment she arrived. The season also included many islanders who delivered captivating television, like Harry Cooksley, Shakira Khan and Helena Ford.
While the UK version is hosted by Maya Jama, it features comedian Iain Stirling as the narrator just like “Love Island USA.”
The current 13th season began June 1, the same week “Love Island USA” Season 8 premiered. However, the UK series runs for eight weeks, meaning the islanders are still in the villa.
Cook says she has already started Season 13 to fill the “Love Island USA” void.
“I couldn’t keep up with both it and Love Island USA at the same time, but now I finally have something to watch every day again,” she says.
‘Vanderpump Rules’ Seasons 1-7, and 9-10
If you want to take a break from reality competition shows but still want an unscripted series, “Vanderpump Rules” is a great option.

The show, which premiered on Bravo in 2013 and focuses on the staff at “The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills” alum Lisa Vanderpump’s restaurants and bars, launched the career of “Love Island USA” host Ariana Madix.
Adrianna shares with TODAY.com that “Vanderpump Rules” is “one of my favorite reality shows ever.”
“If you ever wondered where ‘Love Island USA’ host Ariana Madix got her start, she joins the cast in Season 2,’” she says.
Adrianna acknowledges that the show hits some low points around Season 7.
“But come back for Season 9 to get context before heading straight into ‘Scandoval’ in Season 10,” she says, referencing the major fallout between Madix and ex Tom Sandoval.

title: Beatriz Hatz Didn’t Wear Shorts Until She Was 17. Then She Went on ‘Love Island USA’
summary: Beatriz Hatz discusses her “Love Island USA” experience, hopes for future disability representation on reality TV and training for the Para National Championships.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.
“Love Island USA” Season 8 star Beatriz Hatz is a two-time Paralympian and Paralympic medalist. But unlike most elite athletes, the 25-year-old’s career started as “part of a joke.”
Hatz said on TODAY July 20 she first tried track and field in high school after a challenge from a friend.
“She was like, ‘You beat me at softball, basketball, I know what I can beat you at — track and field,’” Beatriz recalled.

At the time, she was using a walking prosthetic that weighed around five to seven pounds. She agreed to give the sport a chance anyway, motivated in part by the coveted title on the line: “Most Athletic in the Friend Group.”
Beatriz did far more than win the wager. She began competing in increasingly competitive meets, and eventually, she said, “unknowingly” qualified for the World Para Athletics Junior Championships.
“I got a call like, ‘Hey, do you want to represent Team USA?’” she said. “I was 17, and I was like ‘Oh yeah, sure.’”
The Colorado-raised athlete made her debut at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games and won bronze in the women’s 200 meter race at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.

But in June, Beatriz stepped onto a very different stage when she joined Season 8 of “Love Island USA” as a hopeful single. She explored connections with fellow OG islander Sean Reifel and Day 2 bombshell Gabriel Vasconcelos, and ultimately, made franchise history as the first contestant with a visible, physical disability.
On July 23, just weeks after the show wrapped with its July 12 finale, Beatriz is set to compete in the long jump at the Para National Championships in New York.

Speaking with TODAY.com before her interview with Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones, Beatriz opens up about dating with a disability, representing her disability on reality TV and catching up with her fellow islanders after the season finale. Plus, she shares about how she stayed in tip-top shape for her upcoming championship race while in the villa.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

They gave me free range of like, “OK, we’re willing to do what you’re comfortable with. We don’t want to make it a big deal because we chose you for you and not your leg.” Like, “Your leg has nothing to do with why you’re on the show. We really love you, your personality. We think you’re great. Now, like whatever you want to do, like if you want to walk in and act like it’s not a thing, then do that.” And that’s what I did.

I walked in and I was like, well, I don’t really have to say anything because at the end of the day, with all this small talk, it’s like, “Oh, what do you do for work?” And what do I do for work? I’m a professional track and field athlete for the Paralympics. And then it segues into, “Oh, I’m missing my leg.” I think they definitely showed my disability in a way of like “she’s very able to do anything.”

I think there’s a lot of stereotypes that come with disability. You think of somebody that is most likely older, very dependent on somebody else. Most of the time, not in a relationship, most of the time, probably not attractive. But just my existence does break those stigmas, and I think that’s what the world needs to see is that we’re not what you think we are. We’re just people.

Over the years, it’s changed a lot. I was very insecure when I was younger, so I actually didn’t wear shorts in public until I was 17 years old. That was my first time, and now I’m 25, so it’s still not that long ago.

This is probably my third or fourth year with the metal showing on my prosthetics, so it has evolved. When I go to the bar and stuff, and if I’m wearing like pants, it’s not the first thing I say to a guy. “Hey, by the way, I’m missing my leg.” Now if a conversation is going well then it’s like, “Oh, I’m a Paralympian. I do this and this. I’m an amputee,” just to kind of let them know, yeah, I am an amputee, but also I think everybody’s entitled to their preference. I don’t think it’s something to just like spring on somebody.
I took my blade with me. I actually did some training with my blade on. I know they didn’t show it, but I was training.

There’s that little grass patch, so there’s the fire pit, and then there’s all that grass. And I just did a bunch of long jump drills, like repetitive takeoffs, a lot of technical work in the blade, and I did like a tendon ligament circuit, just as much stuff as I could do. And anytime I was called to do something, I’d be running across the villa, just because I did kind of feel a little stir crazy. I was like, I can’t do an actual workout so I’m just gonna run around everywhere.

There was no way to fully keep up with the training the way that it should be done, because my training will take three to four hours, maybe on the track, depending on what we’re doing and how fast or slow we’re going about things. But in the villa, it’s like, you’ve got time to do this, and then you got to go back to doing your other things, like having chats. So I had to be very efficient with the work I was doing.

I have been able to catch up with quite a few of the islanders. I think I’m very excited to see where everybody’s career goes. I think everybody’s so deserving of the love that they’re receiving, and I wish everybody was receiving a lot more love.

The internet is a crazy place, and I don’t think anybody truly knows the islanders the way that we do. And I can’t even say that we know each other super well. Yeah, we spent the summer together, but I wasn’t there for the whole time, anyways. But nobody knows you the way your mom knows you, or your sister knows you, or your best friend knows you, right? And I think that’s something that a lot of people on the internet are forgetting. They think they know us because the TV show does an amazing job of making the viewers think they know you, when in reality, we are very much multifaceted people that have feelings, and I think that that’s one thing that’s missing.

I don’t think I was in a position to really give them advice because they’re definitely going to be in a bigger spotlight. Like they made it to the finals, and they do have a relationship walking out of this. So the only thing that I did give them was love.

Oh my gosh, my DMs are flooded with a bunch of amputees or Latinos or female athletes, and it is really cool to see all the communities that I have touched their hearts, and they’ve seen me on screen and felt that they can relate to me whether they have a disability or not. It’s really cool, but what really is super special to me is when I get messages from young girls that are amputees, and they’re like, “Wow, I’ve been struggling with this.” Or, “You’ve helped me with my confidence.” And those are the messages that I make sure to respond to because it’s like I really wish somebody would have been that for me.

I would just like to see more representation, period. I think people would look at me and would think, oh, she probably is shy or insecure about her leg. But then when I was on the show you could really see me, and people saw, oh, she’s funny, she’s outgoing, she’s doing all these challenges — and I think that’s perfect.

I think more people just need to be given the space and opportunity to even be on screen. I don’t think one person can represent the entire community because we are all different people, but I think it would be really cool to just see more people with disabilities, and especially different kinds. There’s so many disabilities that people don’t know about, and invisible ones at that. My best friend and roommate, she has cerebral palsy. She’s a Paralympian, but people will look at her and be like, “Oh, you’re not disabled.” But then, when you really look at the way like she runs, you’re like, “Oh yeah, you do have a disability.” And I think it’s just like the level of education around disability could definitely go up if there was more representation.

title: Malcolm-Jamal Warner’s Widow Sues His Mother, Successor Trustee, for $1.2 Million in Prenup Dispute
summary: Tenisha Warner, the widow of “The Cosby Show” star Malcolm-Jamal Warner, is suing the late actor’s mother for breach of contract involving the couple’s prenuptial agreement.
story: Tenisha Warner, the widow of “The Cosby Show” star Malcolm-Jamal Warner, is suing the late actor’s mother for breach of contract involving the couple’s prenuptial agreement.

NBC News obtained a copy of the complaint, confirming Tenisha Warner filed the lawsuit on July 20 in the Superior Court of Dekalb County in Georgia. The complaint names mother-in-law Pamela Warner as one of the defendants as she is the successor trustee of the Warner Family Trust. Tenisha Warner alleges in the  suit that she and Malcolm-Jamal Warner — who shared a 9-year-old daughter — married on May 23, 2022, and signed a premarital agreement eight days prior. The lawsuit says Malcolm-Jamal Warner did not fulfill the obligations in the prenup.
Tenisha Warner claims that her late husband “agreed to purchase and maintain a term life insurance policy on his life in the amount of $1,000,000,” with her as the “sole beneficiary.”

But she alleges that the deceased never purchased the life insurance policy for himself or one for her despite the agreement. The complaint also states that Malcom-Jamal Warner agreed to pay his wife $16,000 a year on their anniversary, create a retirement account and pay her a salary of $5,000 per month as his “chief of staff” but failed to do so.
The complaint claims that Tenisha Warner is owed “no less than $1,276,042.46,” plus interest and attorney’s fees and cost.

“Plaintiff performed all obligations required of her under the Agreement, including entering into and remaining in the marriage until the Decedent’s death,” the complaint reads. “The Decedent died without having satisfied his obligations under the Agreement, and no person or entity has paid or provided the sums due to Plaintiff under the Agreement.”

Pamela Warner has been the successor trustee of the Warner Family Trust since Oct. 7, 1996, the document states. The document also lists a “John Doe” as the second defendant because a personal representative has not been named for Malcom-Jamal Warner’s estate.

Additionally, according to the complaint, Tenisha Warner is requesting Pamela Warner, as  successor trustee, be prevented from “distributing, transferring, encumbering, or dissipating” trust property.

“For the last year, I have attempted to privately settle my beloved husband’s complicated estate and honor his last wishes,” Tenisha Warner said in a statement to People. “Malcolm had every intention to provide for our 9-year-old daughter and me. He was close to finalizing a new estate plan to replace the stale plan created in 1996 when he was 26 years old, 20 years before we met and well before we gave birth to our beautiful daughter.”
Tenisha Warner added that her late husband was “unable to do so before we lost him.”

“I have been struggling to care for our daughter as a single mom and now as her sole provider,” she continued. “Legally, I had no choice but to take action to protect our rights before any potential statute of limitations expired. We thank you for your support, love and understanding as we work through this painful process while honoring Malcolm’s life on the first anniversary of his death.”
Reps for Tenisha Warner, Pamela Warner and Malcolm-Jamal Warner’s estate did not immediately return TODAY.com’s request for comment.

Malcolm-Jamal Warner, best known for playing Theo Huxtable as a child star at the start of his decades-long career, died exactly one year before the suit on July 20, 2025, from an accidental drowning in Costa Rica. He was 54.

A representative of Costa Rica’s Judicial Investigation Agency shared a report at the time that said Malcolm-Jamal Warner was swimming at Playa Grande de Cocles when he “apparently was dragged by a current offshore.”
He was rescued and taken to shore where the Costa Rican Red Cross tried to revive him. He was pronounced dead at the scene.
On the anniversary of his death, Pamela Warner penned a letter to her son that was uploaded to his “living legacy” Instagram page.

The message included childhood photos of the “Malcolm & Eddie” star and said, in part, “As I look back, I have no regrets. Perhaps a little more time. Perhaps one more chance to cook his favorite meals, have one last good conversation, one last good deep belly laugh, the kind that produces those tears of pure joy, one last kiss, one last hug.”

She added, “One of the graces in all of this is that we had had healing conversations a few weeks before. We did not know that these were really good-bye conversations. There was nothing left unsaid between us. There was nothing ‘left on the table.’ And I believe that this is why I have been able to be at peace with Malcolm’s transition. I knew beyond a doubt that he loved me and more importantly trusted me. And he knew that I would love him forever and a day.”
Pamela Warner also said that in the past year she has “discovered how cruel, evil and greedy a human can be.”

title: Matt Damon Praises His Female Stunt Double in ‘The Odyssey’: ‘Had the Greatest Arms’
summary: Matt Damon praises his female stunt double that took his place during a vital scene in “The Odyssey.”
story: Matt Damon has called “The Odyssey” the “hardest” and most “challenging” movie he’s ever done, thankfully he had some help from his stunt double.

The 55-year-old actor stars in Christopher Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s epic poem, which follows Odysseus’ grueling journey home after the Trojan War. Along the way, he encounters cyclops, giants and more supernatural beings, all which led to a physically strenuous performance for the actor.
Praised for his physical transformation during a recent interview, Damon took a moment to shine the light on his female stunt double, Devyn Dalton.

“When we did the force perspective stuff of the Laestrygonians... there were these stuntmen who were all 7 feet and then they got stuntmen who were under 5 feet,” Damon told Josh Horowitz on “Happy Sad and Confused” of the scene with the giants. “And so my double was a woman, a female stunt performer, who had the greatest arms I’ve ever seen.”
He recalled meeting Dalton for the first time at a catering tent and embracing her.

“I went up and I hugged her,” Damon said. “And I thanked her for all the work she’d put in.... And there are those shots in the movie where you see these giants looming over me... so it was almost 100% my arms in the movie, but gotta give it up where it’s due.”
In the comments section of Horowitz’s Instagram video, Dalton wrote that it was an “honour to double” for Damon.
In her own Instagram post documenting her personal epic journey as Odysseus, she called the gig “an adventure.”
“Scottish Highlands. The Odyssey. What an adventure. No spoilers just yet, but I’m incredibly grateful to be a part of the Laestrygonian battle,” she wrote.
She added that stunt doubling “the incredible” Damon was “an epic team effort.”

“We worked hard, shared plenty of laughs, and created memories I’ll never forget,” Dalton continued. “The best part of this job is getting to venture to new places and meet amazing people along the way.”
According to Dalton’s impressive IMDB, she is a Canadian born actor, dancer and stunt performer, as well as known for her motion capture performances.
Among her previous credits include “Rise of the Planet of the Apes” and “War for the Planet of the Apes,” “The BFG,” “Scary Movie,” “Descendants: Wicked Wonderland,” “The Last of Us” and many more.

Damon previously shared on Sunday Sitdown that the prep he had to do “as a guy in his 50s” for the film was its “own challenge.” Nolan cautioned him about the extremes that he and the entire “Odyssey” team would face.

“He was like, ‘This movie’s gonna be hard.’ And I looked at him like, ‘I’ve made, I don’t know 80 movies,’” Damon told Willie Geist. “And he goes, ‘No.’ He goes, ‘This movie’s gonna be really hard.’ He, to his credit, was not lying.”

Damon, who also did his own stunts and learned how to use a bow and arrow, shared that the production felt “more like an expedition than a movie,” He added that the entire team, in front of and behind the camera, was “pushed to kind of the limit of what they could do.”
“But the beauty of it is you look around and everyone is going through it with you,” he said.

title: No basic services and nowhere to go: How Venezuelans are living a month after the earthquakes
summary: We visited the ruins of a housing complex built by the Chavista regime: the now homeless residents brave the heat, humidity, and flies from their tents, as they’re promised a house by 2027.
story: LA GUAIRA, Venezuela — A month has passed since earthquakes shook Venezuela and killed thousands, but in the state of La Guaira the old way of life feels like a distant memory.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
Walking through a residential area is like passing through a graveyard of buildings that are no longer recognizable, not even for people who lived there for years.
And then there’s another reality affecting the state: the displaced. Hundreds of people are now living in donated tents after losing their homes.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google
Some still hope the government will help them recover what they’ve lost. Others just want someone to tell them their house can be habitable again.
This is the case at the Brisas de Maiquetía housing development, located directly across from the international airport serving Caracas.

It’s a residential complex built under the Great Housing Mission, the state program created by the late President Hugo Chávez in 2011 to provide social housing to low-income individuals and disaster victims.
Upon entering, one observes a sea of ​​white and blue tarps beneath the once habitable buildings.
Ray Cazorla, a local resident who has lived there for almost 16 years, says the situation is getting worse every day and that the help that has arrived is extremely scarce.

“International aid is not being allowed to pass through here or it is not actually arriving [...] I saw publications showing a truck here with international boxes that were never delivered, it was a lie,” Cazorla told Noticias Telemundo.

The problem intensifies upon entering the tents. The heat, humidity, and steam make it impossible to stay inside. “We barely manage to survive like this. We survive thanks to fans that we had to connect to the power poles, with wiring that we installed ourselves,” Cazorla added.

Previously, residents slept in tents outside the housing complex, but when interim President Delcy Rodríguez visited the area on July 15 to inspect the relief efforts, they were told they had to return to the complex.

Inside, only bunk beds have been provided. Everything else — refrigerators, stoves, gas cylinders, even portable air conditioners— are possessions that families have managed to take from their apartments.

Cazorla explained that he has not been able to remove anything from his house because the stairs were badly cracked by the earthquakes and he fears that if he moves any heavy appliances, the staircase will give way completely.
According to him, the engineers who inspected the buildings said they have no structural problems, only issues with the masonry and brickwork. He doesn’t believe them.
“One of the towers has a broken main beam,” Cazorla said. “I don’t know if they’re going to repair it, but all the apartments are like that.”

Residents say that drinking water doesn’t reach the area. That’s why there are drinking water tanks with filters at various points throughout the development. They weren’t installed by the government, but by the Cadena Foundation, a humanitarian organization of the global Jewish community.
The filtration system, however, has flaws: filling a five-liter pot can take a whole day, since the process works drop by drop.
The remaining tanks — many salvaged from the ruins themselves — are filled with water from the street. Residents say it’s yellow water, unfit for drinking. They only use it for bathing and cooking.
“Every day we feel more alone. The first day the government arrived with a huge crowd, a real commotion, because we thought they were going to make the process quick,” Cazorla said.

Hopes faded when in the following days, he said, no one from from the government showed up and the neighbors were left alone, taking care of their homes and waiting in tents for the nightmare to pass.

The Venezuelan interim government assured them that they could return to their apartments by March 2027. The news wasn’t well received, although some have already resigned themselves to the idea that this tent will be their home for many months. “We’re going to be here for several months; we’re all living on the floor because nobody wants to leave their apartment for fear of having their few valuables stolen,” one person pointed out.
Some people have decorated the entrance to their tents with potted plants, flowers, and family mementos. Others are putting cement underneath them so the soil won’t bother them as much.

Brisas de Maiquetía has not been spared from looting, a problem affecting all of La Guaira. Some buildings have messages painted on their walls: “It’s already been looted” or “Neighbors, be alert, no more looting.” The residents said they themselves had  managed to control the situation, despite having a police post within the area and National Guard troops patrolling.
10 showers for 600 families

The area is home to more than 3,000 people, who must use the public restrooms provided by the state, many of which are poorly maintained. There are 10 public showers that have become unusable over time due to misuse by some residents.
A young couple who lived in the buildings said that they had to repair the showers themselves and are taking point on maintaining them so they’re usable.
“Now there’s no water because the children come unsupervised and use up the whole tank. By the time you go to take a bath, there’s none left,” one of them said.
Cazorla pointed to other daily issues and dangers.
“There are many mosquitoes, many flies. We are prone to the proliferation of cholera or dengue,” he said. “There is stagnant water from the rains and a viral outbreak could occur at any moment.”

Nora Romero, another neighbor, said that some people rush up to their apartments to shower, risking further collapse. The residents are trying to make a living in the ruins because living in the tents isn’t feasible, but the fear is constant: what will happen if an aftershock destroys the buildings?

“The situation is very delicate because there are children. They haven’t even cleared the rubble — we have received some aid, but what we need most is water for the children because diarrhea, flu, and coughs are already an issue,” Romero said.
“We are vulnerable. The stairs have already lost their foundations and are prone to collapse with any aftershock,” said Cazorla.
Rebuild what was broken

Carlos, who prefers not to share his last name, lives on the first floor of one of the towers. His apartment no longer has a kitchen or bathroom, but he and his two children still try to make a life for themselves among the ruins.
“I had just remodeled the apartment. I changed the kitchen, the flooring. Now I’ve lost all of that,” he said. The renovations cost around $2,000, money he knows he won’t get back.

Andrea Debur, who lives on the second floor of the buildings near the entrance to the housing development, said that only the ground floor and first floor apartments — the most affected — will be repaired, while the upper floors, which also suffered some infrastructure damage, were left without a response.

“Officials came to take pictures and then left. They built two walls, and both collapsed. These apartments are uninhabitable; the walls crack more every day,” said Debur, who lives in a tent with her partner, Leonexis Sequeda, and their daughter.
Aid has been scarce. The water from the tanks tastes like chlorine, so they choose to buy water or wait for the donated water to run out before drinking the one from the tanks.
Andrea said that following the earthquake, when they were living outside the housing development on a street across from the airport, they never lacked food.

That changed when Delcy Rodríguez visited the area on July 15th and they were relocated within the housing complex. “Since we’ve been here, they haven’t brought any food. They give us a  government bag, and we get everything else ourselves.”

Debur worked at the airport, which has not yet resumed operations, and is afraid to return. “Without a job, what are we going to do? We’re not saying we’re going to take advantage of the government, but they should help us.”
“It’s so depressing, we want to leave, but the question is where to go? The whole state has been affected. Businesses, supermarkets, pharmacies, banks — there’s nothing left,” Debur said.

According to residents, the governor of La Guaira state, José Alejandro Terán, has visited the neighborhood only twice, but the assistance has not been felt. We contacted the governor’s office for comment, but received no response.

Debur and Sequeda worry about the return to school and work. “I don’t know what condition the high school will be in. I’ve thought about going back to work, but I’m afraid, because all those structures are broken. If we go in there and they don’t fix it properly, there’s going to be another tragedy.”

The residents of Brisas de Maiquetía say they’re asking for only one thing: help. They’re asking the government to address the basic needs of the community and for the international community not to turn a blind eye.
Aside from rubble and collapsed buildings, the earthquake left behind people, who hope they won’t be forgotten.
An earlier version of this story was first published in Noticias Telemundo.

title: U.S. launches new strikes and Trump threatens ‘massive attack’ as Iran widens war
summary: The United States launched a fresh barrage of strikes on Iran overnight as President Donald Trump threatened a major new escalation after Tehran opened a second front in its pressure campaign on the world economy.
story: JERUSALEM — The United States launched a fresh barrage of strikes on Iran overnight after Tehran opened a second front in its pressure campaign on the world economy.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

President Donald Trump threatened a major new escalation and on Thursday told Axios he is weighing whether to launch a “massive attack” on the Islamic Republic that would be “bigger than ever before.” The president’s warning and subsequent 13th night of military strikes came as oil briefly surged above $100 a barrel.
Though Trump appeared to leave the door open for a diplomatic solution in comments to reporters on Friday afternoon.

“There’s two ways. I mean, it’s, you can just keep doing exactly what we’re doing and take them apart piece by piece. We could do it in a more rapid fashion, which we might do, or we can negotiate with them, which we’re also doing right now,” Trump told a gathering of reporters at the White House. “I mean, as we speak, we’re talking to them.”

Iran has shown little sign of bowing to U.S. demands, launching new attacks on shipping as well as U.S. bases and allies across the Middle East. These two fronts have combined to increase the cost of the renewed conflict — in human lives, including American soldiers, and global prices.
The struggle for control of the crucial Strait of Hormuz has now been extended to another key trade route, the Bab el Mandeb strait, after attacks by Tehran-backed Houthi rebels in the Red Sea.

And there were signs that some U.S. partners in the region may be losing patience. Senior Arab officials told NBC News they were growing frustrated with the threats, the daily escalations and the lack of diplomatic progress.

“We have no clue where this is going,” said one senior Arab official, with direct knowledge of regional developments. “It’s only getting crazier,” said another senior Arab official, directly involved with diplomatic efforts.

title: Oil prices surge to $100 per barrel after Red Sea attacks
summary: European and U.S. crude oil both jumped, hitting their highest levels in weeks.
story: Oil prices rose Thursday to their highest levels in nearly two months after the latest Iran war escalation threatened severe new disruptions to global energy supplies.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Brent crude oil, one of two key global benchmarks, closed higher by 7%, at $100.69 per barrel. Earlier in the trading day, it rose as high as $102 per barrel. That is its highest level in eight weeks, since the end of May.
U.S. crude oil also jumped for a second straight day, closing higher by 6.2%, at $92.19 per barrel — its highest close since June 4.
The prices surged after Tehran-backed Houthi rebels claimed attacks on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea following their announcement of a naval blockade on the kingdom.
